1.39.m: Extremely fierce, with venom in their sight, of fiery wrath, difficult to approach, / hundreds of great uragas are there, obedient to Suvarṇa. 39.35

1.39.s:
sunāge'pi mahāśaile daityāvāsā- sahasraśaḥ.
harmyaprāsāda kalilāḥ prāṃśuprākāratoraṇāḥ .. 39.36 ..
1.39.d:
सुनागेऽपि महाशैले दैत्यावासा- सहस्रशः।
हर्म्यप्रासाद कलिलाः प्रांशुप्राकारतोरणाः ॥ 39.36 ॥
1.39.m: On the great mountain Sunāga, too, are dwellings of the daityas by the thousands, / packed with mansions and palaces, with high ramparts and archways. 39.36

1.39.s:
veṇumante mahāśaile vidyādharapuratrayam.
triṃśadadyojanavistīrṇaṃ pañcāśadyojanāyatam .. 39.37 ..
1.39.d:
वेणुमन्ते महाशैले विद्याधरपुरत्रयम्।
त्रिंशदद्योजनविस्तीर्णं पञ्चाशद्योजनायतम् ॥ 39.37 ॥
1.39.m: On the great mountain Veṇumant is a triad of cities of the vidyādharas, / thirty yojanas broad and fifty yojanas long. 39.37

1.39.s:
ulūko romaśaścaiva mahānetraśca vīryavān.
vidyādharavarāstatra śakratulyaparākramāḥ .. 39.38 ..
1.39.d:
उलूको रोमशश्चैव महानेत्रश्च वीर्यवान्।
विद्याधरवरास्तत्र शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः ॥ 39.38 ॥
1.39.m: Ulūka, Romaśa, and the heroic Mahānetra— / there dwell the best of vidyādharas, equal in prowess to Śakra. 39.38

1.39.s:
vaikaṅke śailaśikhare hyantaḥkandaranirjhare.
mahoccaśrṛṅge rucire ratnadhātuvicitrite .. 39.39 ..
1.39.d:
वैकङ्के शैलशिखरे ह्यन्तःकन्दरनिर्झरे।
महोच्चश्रृङ्गे रुचिरे रत्नधातुविचित्रिते ॥ 39.39 ॥
1.39.m: On the mountain summit of Vaikaṅka, with waterfalls in the depths of its caves, / on a very lofty, delightful peak variegated with gems and minerals, 39.39

1.39.s:
tatrāste gāruḍirnityaṃ uragārirdurāsadaḥ.
mahāvāyujavaścaṇḍaḥ sugrīvo nāma vīryavān .. 39.40 ..
1.39.d:
तत्रास्ते गारुडिर्नित्यं उरगारिर्दुरासदः।
महावायुजवश्चण्डः सुग्रीवो नाम वीर्यवान् ॥ 39.40 ॥
1.39.m: there dwells constantly the heroic son of Garuḍa, the enemy of uragas, difficult to approach, / fierce, having the speed of a great wind, Sugrīva by name. 39.40

1.39.s:
mahāpramāṇai rvikrāntairmahābalaparākramaiḥ.
saśailo hyāvṛtaḥ sarvaḥ pakṣibhiḥ pannagāribhiḥ .. 39.41 ..
1.39.d:
महाप्रमाणै र्विक्रान्तैर्महाबलपराक्रमैः।
सशैलो ह्यावृतः सर्वः पक्षिभिः पन्नगारिभिः ॥ 39.41 ॥
1.39.m: That mountain is entirely encircled by birds of great measure, / valorous, of great strength and prowess, enemies of the pannagas. 39.41

1.39.s:
karañje'bhirato nityaṃ sākṣādbhūtapatiḥ prabhuḥ.
vṛṣabhāṅko mahādevaḥ śaṅkaro yogināṃ prabhuḥ .. 39.42 ..
1.39.d:
करञ्जेऽभिरतो नित्यं साक्षाद्भूतपतिः प्रभुः।
वृषभाङ्को महादेवः शङ्करो योगिनां प्रभुः ॥ 39.42 ॥
1.39.m: On Mount Karañja, the Lord, the master of bhūtas, constantly delights in person— / Mahādeva, whose emblem is the bull, Śaṅkara, the lord of yogins. 39.42

1.39.s:
nānāveṣadharairbhūtaiḥ pramathaiśca durāsadaiḥ.
karañje sānavaḥ sarve hyavakīrṇāḥ samantataḥ .. 39.43 ..
1.39.d:
नानावेषधरैर्भूतैः प्रमथैश्च दुरासदैः।
करञ्जे सानवः सर्वे ह्यवकीर्णाः समन्ततः ॥ 39.43 ॥
1.39.m: With bhūtas wearing diverse attires and unassailable pramathas, / all the peaks on Karañja are strewn on every side. 39.43

1.39.s:
vasudhāre vasumatāṃ vasūnāmamitaujasām.
aṣṭāvāyatanānyāhuḥ pūjitāni mahātmanām .. 39.44 ..
1.39.d:
वसुधारे वसुमतां वसूनाममितौजसाम्।
अष्टावायतनान्याहुः पूजितानि महात्मनाम् ॥ 39.44 ॥
1.39.m: On Mount Vasudhāra, they say, are eight honored abodes / of the rich Vasus of boundless splendour, the great-souled ones. 39.44

1.39.s:
ratnadhātau girivare ṛṣīṇāñca mahātmanām.
saptāśramāṇi puṇyāni siddhāvāsayutāni ca .. 39.45 ..
1.39.d:
रत्नधातौ गिरिवरे ऋषीणाञ्च महात्मनाम्।
सप्ताश्रमाणि पुण्यानि सिद्धावासयुतानि च ॥ 39.45 ॥
1.39.m: On the excellent mountain Ratnadhātu are seven sacred hermitages / of the great-souled seers, joined with the dwellings of siddhas. 39.45

1.39.s:
mahāprajāpateḥ sthānaṃ hemaśrṛṅgo nagottame.
caturvaktrasya devasya sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam .. 30.46 ..
1.39.d:
महाप्रजापतेः स्थानं हेमश्रृङ्गो नगोत्तमे।
चतुर्वक्त्रस्य देवस्य सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम् ॥ 30.46 ॥
1.39.m: On the best of mountains, Hemaśṛṅga, is the abode of the Great Prajāpati, / the four-faced god, saluted by all living beings. 39.46

1.39.s:
gajaśaile bhagavato nānābhūtagaṇāvṛtāḥ .
rudrāḥ pramuditā nityaṃ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtāḥ .. 39.47 ..
1.39.d:
गजशैले भगवतो नानाभूतगणावृताः ।
रुद्राः प्रमुदिता नित्यं सर्वभूतनमस्कृताः ॥ 39.47 ॥
1.39.m: On the Gaja mountain, the joyous Rudras of the Lord, surrounded by host of various beings, / are eternally bowed to by all creatures.

1.39.s:
sumedhe dhātucitrāḍhye śailendre meghasannibhe.
naikodaradarīvapranikuñjaiścopaśobhite .. 39.48 ..
1.39.d:
सुमेधे धातुचित्राढ्ये शैलेन्द्रे मेघसन्निभे।
नैकोदरदरीवप्रनिकुञ्जैश्चोपशोभिते ॥ 39.48 ॥
1.39.m: On Sumedha, richly adorned with varied minerals, a king of mountains resembling a cloud, / adorned with many internal caves, valleys, slopes, and bowers,

1.39.s:
ādityānāṃ vasūnāñca rudrāṇāñcāmitaujasām.
tatrāyatanavinyāsā ramyāścaivāśvinorapi .. 39.49 ..
1.39.d:
आदित्यानां वसूनाञ्च रुद्राणाञ्चामितौजसाम्।
तत्रायतनविन्यासा रम्याश्चैवाश्विनोरपि ॥ 39.49 ॥
1.39.m: there are delightful layouts of temples of the Ādityas, Vasus, / and Rudras of boundless splendour, and also of the two Aśvins.

1.39.s:
sthānāni siddhairdevānāṃ sthāpitāni nagottame.
tatra pūjāparā nityaṃ yakṣa gandharvakinnarāḥ .. 39.50 ..
1.39.d:
स्थानानि सिद्धैर्देवानां स्थापितानि नगोत्तमे।
तत्र पूजापरा नित्यं यक्ष गन्धर्वकिन्नराः ॥ 39.50 ॥
1.39.m: These abodes of the gods were established by the siddhas upon that best of mountains; / there, yakṣas, gandharvas, and kinnaras are ever devoted to their worship.

1.39.s:
gandharvanagarī sphītā hemakakṣe nagottame.
aśītyāmarapuryyābhā mahāprākāratoraṇā .. 39.51 ..
1.39.d:
गन्धर्वनगरी स्फीता हेमकक्षे नगोत्तमे।
अशीत्यामरपुर्य्याभा महाप्राकारतोरणा ॥ 39.51 ॥
1.39.m: On Hemakakṣa, the best of mountains, there is a prosperous city of gandharvas, / eighty [yojanas wide], resembling the city of the immortals, with great ramparts and archways.

1.39.s:
siddhā hyapattanā nāma gandharvā yuddha śālinaḥ.
yeṣāmadhipatirdevo rājarājaḥ kapiñjalaḥ .. 39.52 ..
1.39.d:
सिद्धा ह्यपत्तना नाम गन्धर्वा युद्ध शालिनः।
येषामधिपतिर्देवो राजराजः कपिञ्जलः ॥ 39.52 ॥
1.39.m: There dwell the accomplished gandharvas skilled in battle, known as the Apattanas, / whose sovereign lord is the god, the king of kings, Kapiñjala.

1.39.s:
anale rākṣasāvāsāḥ pañcakūṭe'pi dānavāḥ.
ūrjitā devaripavo mahābalaparākramāḥ .. 39.53 ..
1.39.d:
अनले राक्षसावासाः पञ्चकूटेऽपि दानवाः।
ऊर्जिता देवरिपवो महाबलपराक्रमाः ॥ 39.53 ॥
1.39.m: On Anala are the dwellings of rākṣasas, and on Pañcakūṭa are the dānavas, / mighty enemies of the gods, possessing great strength and prowess.

1.39.s:
śataśrṛṅge puraśataṃ yakṣāṇāmamitaujasām.
tāmrābhe kādraveyasya takṣakasya purottamam .. 39.54 ..
1.39.d:
शतश्रृङ्गे पुरशतं यक्षाणाममितौजसाम्।
ताम्राभे काद्रवेयस्य तक्षकस्य पुरोत्तमम् ॥ 39.54 ॥
1.39.m: On Śataśṛṅga there is a hundred cities of yakṣas of boundless splendour; / on Tāmrābha is the supreme city of Kadrū's son, Takṣaka.

1.39.s:
viśākhe parvataśreṣṭhe naikavapradarīśubhe.
guhāniratavāsasya guhasyāyatanaṃ mahat .. 39.55 ..
1.39.d:
विशाखे पर्वतश्रेष्ठे नैकवप्रदरीशुभे।
गुहानिरतवासस्य गुहस्यायतनं महत् ॥ 39.55 ॥
1.39.m: On Viśākha, the best of mountains, beautiful with many slopes and caves, / is the great abode of Guha, who delights in dwelling in caves.

1.39.s:
śvetodare mahāśaile mahābhavanamaṇḍite.
puraṃ garuḍhaputrasya sunābhasya mahātmanaḥ .. 39.56 ..
1.39.d:
श्वेतोदरे महाशैले महाभवनमण्डिते।
पुरं गरुढपुत्रस्य सुनाभस्य महात्मनः ॥ 39.56 ॥
1.39.m: On the great mountain Śvetodara, adorned with great mansions, / is the city of the high-souled Sunābha, son of Garuḍa.

1.39.s:
piśācake girivare harmyaṃ prāsāda maṇḍitam.
yakṣagandharvacaritaṃ kuberabhavanaṃ mahat .. 30.57 ..
1.39.d:
पिशाचके गिरिवरे हर्म्यं प्रासाद मण्डितम्।
यक्षगन्धर्वचरितं कुबेरभवनं महत् ॥ 30.57 ॥
1.39.m: On the excellent mountain Piśācaka, there is an edifice adorned with palaces, / frequented by yakṣas and gandharvas—the great mansion of Kubera.

1.39.s:
harikūṭe harirdevaḥ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtaḥ.
prabhāvāttasya śailo'sau mahānābhaḥ prakāśate .. 39.58 ..
1.39.d:
हरिकूटे हरिर्देवः सर्वभूतनमस्कृतः।
प्रभावात्तस्य शैलोऽसौ महानाभः प्रकाशते ॥ 39.58 ॥
1.39.m: On Harikūṭa is the god Hari, revered by all creatures; / through his majesty that great mountain shines forth, resembling the sky.

1.39.s:
kumude kinnarāvāsā añjane ca mahoragāḥ.
kṛṣṇe gandharvvanagarā mahābhavanaśālinaḥ .. 39.59 ..
1.39.d:
कुमुदे किन्नरावासा अञ्जने च महोरगाः।
कृष्णे गन्धर्व्वनगरा महाभवनशालिनः ॥ 39.59 ॥
1.39.m: On Kumuda are the abodes of kinnaras, and on Añjana the great uragas; / on Kṛṣṇa are the gandharva cities endowed with great mansions.

1.39.s:
pāṇḍure cāruśikhare mahāprākāratoraṇe.
vidyādharapuraṃ tatra mahābhavanamālinam .. 39.60 ..
1.39.d:
पाण्डुरे चारुशिखरे महाप्राकारतोरणे।
विद्याधरपुरं तत्र महाभवनमालिनम् ॥ 39.60 ॥
1.39.m: On Pāṇḍura, with its beautiful peak and great ramparts and archways, / is the city of the vidyādharas, garlanded with magnificent mansions.

1.39.s:
sahasraśikhare śaile daityānāmugrakarmmaṇām.
purāṇi samudīrṇānāṃ sahasraṃ hemamālinām .. 39.61 ..
1.39.d:
सहस्रशिखरे शैले दैत्यानामुग्रकर्म्मणाम्।
पुराणि समुदीर्णानां सहस्रं हेममालिनाम् ॥ 39.61 ॥
1.39.m: On the mountain Sahasraśikhara, there are a thousand cities of the daityas / of fierce deeds, towering high and garlanded in gold.

1.39.s:
mukuṭe pannagāvāsā anekāḥ parvatottamāḥ.
puṣpake vai munigaṇā nityameva mudā yutāḥ .. 39.62 ..
1.39.d:
मुकुटे पन्नगावासा अनेकाः पर्वतोत्तमाः।
पुष्पके वै मुनिगणा नित्यमेव मुदा युताः ॥ 39.62 ॥
1.39.m: On Mukuṭa are many best of mountains that are the abodes of pannagas; / on Puṣpaka, hosts of munis dwell, ever filled with joy.

1.39.s:
vaivasvatasya somasya vāyornāgādhipasya ca.
supakṣe parvatavare catvāryyāyatanāni ca .. 39.63 ..
1.39.d:
वैवस्वतस्य सोमस्य वायोर्नागाधिपस्य च।
सुपक्षे पर्वतवरे चत्वार्य्यायतनानि च ॥ 39.63 ॥
1.39.m: On Supakṣa, the best of mountains, are the four abodes / of Vaivasvata, Soma, Vāyu, and the lord of serpents.

1.39.s:
gandharvaiḥ kinnarairyakṣairnnāgairvidyādharottamaiḥ.
siddhairhi teṣu sthāneṣu nityamiṣṭaḥ prapūjyate .. 39.64 ..
1.39.d:
गन्धर्वैः किन्नरैर्यक्षैर्न्नागैर्विद्याधरोत्तमैः।
सिद्धैर्हि तेषु स्थानेषु नित्यमिष्टः प्रपूज्यते ॥ 39.64 ॥
1.39.m: In those places, the desired [deity] is constantly worshipped / by gandharvas, kinnaras, yakṣas, nāgas, the best of vidyādharas, and siddhas.

1.39.s: iti śrīmahā purāṇe vāyuprokte bhuvanavinyāso nāmaikonacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 39 ..
1.39.d: इति श्रीमहा पुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते भुवनविन्यासो नामैकोनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 39 ॥
1.39.m: Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Arrangement of the Earth," in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.40.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.40.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.40.m:
The Sūta said:
Learn of Devakūṭa, the bright boundary mountain,
on the broad summit, on the peak of that best of mountains.

1.40.s:
maryyādāparvate śubhre devakūṭe nibodhata.
vistīrṇe sikhare tasya kūṭe girivarasya ha .. 40.1 ..
1.40.d:
मर्य्यादापर्वते शुभ्रे देवकूटे निबोधत।
विस्तीर्णे सिखरे तस्य कूटे गिरिवरस्य ह ॥ 40.1 ॥

1.40.s:
samantādyojanaśataṃ mahābhavanamaṇḍitam.
janmakṣetraṃ suparṇasya vainateyasya dhīmataḥ .. 40.2 ..
1.40.d:
समन्ताद्योजनशतं महाभवनमण्डितम्।
जन्मक्षेत्रं सुपर्णस्य वैनतेयस्य धीमतः ॥ 40.2 ॥
1.40.m: measuring a hundred yojanas all around, adorned with great mansions, / is the birthplace of Suparṇa, the wise son of Vinatā,

1.40.s:
naikairmahā pakṣigaṇairgāruḍaiḥ śīgravikramaiḥ.
sampūrṇavīryasampannairdamanairuragāribhiḥ .. 40.3 ..
1.40.d:
नैकैर्महा पक्षिगणैर्गारुडैः शीग्रविक्रमैः।
सम्पूर्णवीर्यसम्पन्नैर्दमनैरुरगारिभिः ॥ 40.3 ॥
1.40.m: filled with numerous hosts of great birds born of Garuḍa, swift in their stride, / endowed with full prowess, tamers [of foes], enemies of serpents.

1.40.s:
pakṣirājasya bhavanaṃ prathamaṃ tanmahātmanaḥ.
mahāvāyupraveśasya śālmali dvīpavāsinaḥ .. 40.4 ..
1.40.d:
पक्षिराजस्य भवनं प्रथमं तन्महात्मनः।
महावायुप्रवेशस्य शाल्मलि द्वीपवासिनः ॥ 40.4 ॥
1.40.m: That is the primeval mansion of the high-souled king of birds, / who moves like a great wind and dwells on Śālmalidvīpa.

1.40.s:
tasyaiva cārumūrdhnastu kūṭeṣu ca maharddhiṣu.
dakṣiṇeṣu vicitreṣu saptasvapi tu śobhinaḥ .. 40.5 ..
1.40.d:
तस्यैव चारुमूर्ध्नस्तु कूटेषु च महर्द्धिषु।
दक्षिणेषु विचित्रेषु सप्तस्वपि तु शोभिनः ॥ 40.5 ॥
1.40.m: On the beautiful crest of that very mountain, upon its seven southern peaks, / glorious, possessing great fortune, and wonderful,

1.40.s:
sandhyābhrābhāḥ samuditā rukmaprākāratoraṇāḥ.
mahābhavanamālābhiḥ śobhitā devanirmitāḥ .. 40.6 ..
1.40.d:
सन्ध्याभ्राभाः समुदिता रुक्मप्राकारतोरणाः।
महाभवनमालाभिः शोभिता देवनिर्मिताः ॥ 40.6 ॥
1.40.m: there are [cities] built by the gods, resembling evening clouds, prosperous, / with ramparts and archways of gold, adorned with rows of great mansions,

1.40.s:
triṃśadyojanavistīrṇāścatvāriṃśattamāyatāḥ.
sapta gandharvanagarā nara nārīsamākulāḥ .. 40.7 ..
1.40.d:
त्रिंशद्योजनविस्तीर्णाश्चत्वारिंशत्तमायताः।
सप्त गन्धर्वनगरा नर नारीसमाकुलाः ॥ 40.7 ॥
1.40.m: thirty yojanas in width and forty in length— / seven cities of the gandharvas, thronged with men and women.

1.40.s:
āgneyā nāma gandharvā mahābalaparākramāḥ.
kuberānucarā dīptāsteṣānte bhavanottamāḥ .. 40.8 ..
1.40.d:
आग्नेया नाम गन्धर्वा महाबलपराक्रमाः।
कुबेरानुचरा दीप्तास्तेषान्ते भवनोत्तमाः ॥ 40.8 ॥
1.40.m: Those excellent mansions belong to the blazing gandharvas named Āgneyas, / followers of Kubera, endowed with great strength and valor.

1.40.s:
tasya cottarakūṭeṣu bhuvanasya mahāgireḥ.
harmyaprāsādabaddhaṃ ca udyānavanaśobhitam .. 40.9 ..
1.40.d:
तस्य चोत्तरकूटेषु भुवनस्य महागिरेः।
हर्म्यप्रासादबद्धं च उद्यानवनशोभितम् ॥ 40.9 ॥
1.40.m: And on the northern peaks of that mountain of the world, / built with mansions and palaces, adorned with gardens and groves,

1.40.s:
puramāśīviṣaiḥ purṇaṃ mahāprākāratoraṇam.
vāditraśatanirghoṣairānanditavanāntaram .. 40.10 ..
1.40.d:
पुरमाशीविषैः पुर्णं महाप्राकारतोरणम्।
वादित्रशतनिर्घोषैरानन्दितवनान्तरम् ॥ 40.10 ॥
1.40.m: is a city filled with venomous serpents, with great ramparts and gateways, / its forest glades delighted by the resonant sounds of hundreds of musical instruments,

1.40.s:
duṣprasahyamamitrāṇāṃ triṃśadyojanamaṇḍalam.
nagaraṃ saiṃhikeyānāmudīrṇaṃ devavidviṣām.
siddhadevarṣicaritaṃ devakūṭe nibodhata .. 40.11 ..
1.40.d:
दुष्प्रसह्यममित्राणां त्रिंशद्योजनमण्डलम्।
नगरं सैंहिकेयानामुदीर्णं देवविद्विषाम्।
सिद्धदेवर्षिचरितं देवकूटे निबोधत ॥ 40.11 ॥
1.40.m: insufferable to enemies, thirty yojanas in circumference— / a haughty city of the sons of Siṃhikā, the haters of the gods, / frequented by siddhas and celestial seers; know it to be on Devakūṭa.

1.40.s:
dvitīye dvijaśārdūla maryyādāparvate śubhe.
mahābhavanamālābhirnānāvarṇābhirāvṛtam .. 40.12 ..
1.40.d:
द्वितीये द्विजशार्दूल मर्य्यादापर्वते शुभे।
महाभवनमालाभिर्नानावर्णाभिरावृतम् ॥ 40.12 ॥
1.40.m: On the second auspicious boundary-mountain, O tiger among the twice-born, / covered with rows of great mansions of diverse colors,

1.40.s:
suvarṇamaṇicitrābhiranekābhiralaṃkṛtam .
viśālarathyaṃ durdharṣaṃ nityaṃ pramuditaṃ śivam .. 40.13 ..
1.40.d:
सुवर्णमणिचित्राभिरनेकाभिरलंकृतम् ।
विशालरथ्यं दुर्धर्षं नित्यं प्रमुदितं शिवम् ॥ 40.13 ॥
1.40.m: adorned with many [palaces] glistening with gold and gems, / with broad streets, invincible, ever joyous and auspicious,

1.40.s:
naranārīgaṇākīrṇaṃ prāṃśuprākāratoraṇam .
ṣaṣṭiyojanavistīrṇaṃ śatayojanamāyatam .. 40.14 ..
1.40.d:
नरनारीगणाकीर्णं प्रांशुप्राकारतोरणम् ।
षष्टियोजनविस्तीर्णं शतयोजनमायतम् ॥ 40.14 ॥
1.40.m: thronged with crowds of men and women, with lofty ramparts and gateways, / sixty yojanas in width and a hundred yojanas in length,

1.40.s:
nagaraṃ kālakeyānāmasurāṇāṃ durāsadam.
devakūṭataṭe ramye sanniviṣṭaṃ sudurjayam.
mahābhracayasaṅkāśaṃ sunāsannāma viśrutam .. 40.15 ..
1.40.d:
नगरं कालकेयानामसुराणां दुरासदम्।
देवकूटतटे रम्ये सन्निविष्टं सुदुर्जयम्।
महाभ्रचयसङ्काशं सुनासन्नाम विश्रुतम् ॥ 40.15 ॥
1.40.m: is the city of the Kālakeya asuras, difficult to approach, / situated on a delightful slope of Devakūṭa, exceedingly hard to conquer, / resembling a gathering of huge clouds, renowned by the name of Sunāsa.

1.40.s:
tasyaiva dakṣiṇe kūṭe viṃśadyojanavistaram.
dviṣaṣṭiyojanāyāmaṃ hemaprākāratoraṇam .. 40.16 ..
1.40.d:
तस्यैव दक्षिणे कूटे विंशद्योजनविस्तरम्।
द्विषष्टियोजनायामं हेमप्राकारतोरणम् ॥ 40.16 ॥
1.40.m: On the southern peak of that very [mountain], twenty yojanas in width / and sixty-two yojanas in length, with golden ramparts and archways,

1.40.s:
hṛṣṭapuṣṭāvaliptānāmāvāsāḥ kāmarūpiṇām.
autkacānāṃ pramuditaṃ rākṣasānāṃ mahāpuram .. 40.17 ..
1.40.d:
हृष्टपुष्टावलिप्तानामावासाः कामरूपिणाम्।
औत्कचानां प्रमुदितं राक्षसानां महापुरम् ॥ 40.17 ॥
1.40.m: is the dwelling of those who assume forms at will, joyful, plump, and haughty— / the delighted, great city of the Autkaca rākṣasas.

1.40.s:
madhyame tu mahākūṭe devakūṭasya vai gireḥ .
suvarṇamaṇipāṣāṇaiścitraiḥ ślakṣaṇataraiḥ śubhaiḥ.
śākhāśatasahasrādyairnaikārohasamākulam .. 40.18 ..
1.40.d:
मध्यमे तु महाकूटे देवकूटस्य वै गिरेः ।
सुवर्णमणिपाषाणैश्चित्रैः श्लक्षणतरैः शुभैः।
शाखाशतसहस्राद्यैर्नैकारोहसमाकुलम् ॥ 40.18 ॥
1.40.m: Upon the central great peak of Mount Devakūṭa, / [surrounded] by variegated, very smooth, beautiful rocks of gold and jewels, / filled with hundreds of thousands of branches and multiple aerial roots,

1.40.s:
srigdha parṇamahāmūlamanekaskandhavāhanam.
ramyaṃ hyaviralacchāyaṃ daśayojanamaṇḍalam .. 40.19 ..
1.40.d:
स्रिग्ध पर्णमहामूलमनेकस्कन्धवाहनम्।
रम्यं ह्यविरलच्छायं दशयोजनमण्डलम् ॥ 40.19 ॥
1.40.m: having glossy leaves and great roots, supporting multiple trunks, / delightful, with unbroken shade, ten yojanas in circumference,

1.40.s:
tatra bhūtavaṭannāma nānābhūtagaṇālayam.
mahādevasya prathitaṃ tryambakasya mahātmanaḥ.
dīptamāyatanaṃ tatra sarvalokeṣu viśrutam .. 40.20 ..
1.40.d:
तत्र भूतवटन्नाम नानाभूतगणालयम्।
महादेवस्य प्रथितं त्र्यम्बकस्य महात्मनः।
दीप्तमायतनं तत्र सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतम् ॥ 40.20 ॥
1.40.m: stands the celebrated banyan known as Bhūtavaṭa, the abode of diverse hosts of bhūtas, / the blazing shrine of the great-souled Mahādeva Tryambaka, / famous throughout all the worlds.

1.40.s:
varāhagajasiṃharkṣaśārdūlakarabhānanaiḥ.
gṛdhrolūkamukhaiścaiva meṣoṣṭrājamahāmukhaiḥ .. 40.21 ..
1.40.d:
वराहगजसिंहर्क्षशार्दूलकरभाननैः।
गृध्रोलूकमुखैश्चैव मेषोष्ट्राजमहामुखैः ॥ 40.21 ॥
1.40.m: With faces like boars, elephants, lions, bears, tigers, and young camels, / with faces like vultures and owls, and great faces like sheep, camels, and goats,

1.40.s:
kadambairvikaṭaiḥ sthūlairlambakeśatanūruhaiḥ.
nānāvarṇākṛtidharairnānāsaṃsthānasaṃsthitaiḥ .. 40.22 ..
1.40.d:
कदम्बैर्विकटैः स्थूलैर्लम्बकेशतनूरुहैः।
नानावर्णाकृतिधरैर्नानासंस्थानसंस्थितैः ॥ 40.22 ॥
1.40.m: in large groups, monstrous, gross, with trailing hair and body hair, / bearing varied colors and shapes, abiding in diverse postures,

1.40.s:
dīptairanekairugrāsyairbhūtairugraparākramaiḥ.
aśūnyamabhavannityaṃ mahāpāriṣadaistathā .. 40.23 ..
1.40.d:
दीप्तैरनेकैरुग्रास्यैर्भूतैरुग्रपराक्रमैः।
अशून्यमभवन्नित्यं महापारिषदैस्तथा ॥ 40.23 ॥
1.40.m: blazing, numerous, with dreadful jaws, bhūtas of terrible prowess, / and likewise with great attendants, it is never unoccupied.

1.40.s:
tatra bhūtapaterbhūtā nityampūjāṃ prayuñjate.
jharjharaiḥ śaṅkhapaṭahairbherīḍiṇḍimagomukhaiḥ .. 40.24 ..
1.40.d:
तत्र भूतपतेर्भूता नित्यम्पूजां प्रयुञ्जते।
झर्झरैः शङ्खपटहैर्भेरीडिण्डिमगोमुखैः ॥ 40.24 ॥
1.40.m: There the bhūtas continually offer worship to the Lord of Bhūtas / with jharjharas, conches, paṭahas, bherīs, ḍiṇḍimas, and gomukhas,

1.40.s:
raṇitālasitodgītai rnityaṃ valitavarjitaiḥ.
visphūrjjitaśataistatra pūjāyuktā gaṇeśvarāḥ.
prītāḥ purāripramathāstatra krīḍāparāḥ sadā .. 40.25 ..
1.40.d:
रणितालसितोद्गीतै र्नित्यं वलितवर्जितैः।
विस्फूर्ज्जितशतैस्तत्र पूजायुक्ता गणेश्वराः।
प्रीताः पुरारिप्रमथास्तत्र क्रीडापराः सदा ॥ 40.25 ॥
1.40.m: with musical sounds, graceful loud singing, ever devoid of hesitation, / and hundreds of roars; engaged in worship there, the lords of the gaṇas, / the pramathas of the Enemy of Pura, are ever delighted and devoted to sport.

1.40.s:
siddhadevarṣigandharvayakṣanāgendra pūjitaḥ.
sthāne tasmin mahādevaḥ sākṣāllokaśivaḥ śivaḥ .. 40.26 ..
1.40.d:
सिद्धदेवर्षिगन्धर्वयक्षनागेन्द्र पूजितः।
स्थाने तस्मिन् महादेवः साक्षाल्लोकशिवः शिवः ॥ 40.26 ॥
1.40.m: Worshipped by siddhas, divine seers, gandharvas, yakṣas, and serpent-lords, / in that abode stands Mahādeva, the embodiment of Śiva, bringing welfare to the world.

1.40.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte bhuvanavinyāso nāma catvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 40 ..
1.40.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते भुवनविन्यासो नाम चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 40 ॥
1.40.m: Thus ends the fortieth chapter, named “The Arrangement of the Earth,” in the holy Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.41.s: ..sūta uvāca ..
1.41.d: ॥सूत उवाच ॥

1.41.s:
viviktacāruśikharaṃ patritaṃ śaṅkhavarcasam.
kailāsaṃ devabhaktānāmālayaṃ sukṛtātmanām .. 41.1 ..
1.41.d:
विविक्तचारुशिखरं पत्रितं शङ्खवर्चसम्।
कैलासं देवभक्तानामालयं सुकृतात्मनाम् ॥ 41.1 ॥

1.41.s:
tasya kūṭataṭe ramye madhyame kundasannibhe.
yojanānāṃ śatāyāme pañcāśacca tathāyatam .. 42.2 ..
1.41.d:
तस्य कूटतटे रम्ये मध्यमे कुन्दसन्निभे।
योजनानां शतायामे पञ्चाशच्च तथायतम् ॥ 42.2 ॥
1.41.m: On its delightful middle ridge, resembling a kunda flower, / one hundred yojanas in length and fifty broad,

1.41.s:
suvarṇamaṇicitrābhi anekābhiralaṃkṛtam.
mahābhavanamālābhirbhūṣitaṃ naikavistaram .. 41.3 ..
1.41.d:
सुवर्णमणिचित्राभि अनेकाभिरलंकृतम्।
महाभवनमालाभिर्भूषितं नैकविस्तरम् ॥ 41.3 ॥
1.41.m: adorned with numerous wonders of gold and gems, / decorated with rows of great mansions of manifold extent,

1.41.s:
dhanādhyakṣasya devasya kuberasya mahātmanaḥ.
nagarantadanādhṛṣyamṛddhiyuktaṃ mudāyutam .. 41.4 ..
1.41.d:
धनाध्यक्षस्य देवस्य कुबेरस्य महात्मनः।
नगरन्तदनाधृष्यमृद्धियुक्तं मुदायुतम् ॥ 41.4 ॥
1.41.m: is the invincible city of the great-souled god Kubera, / the lord of wealth, endowed with abundance and full of joy.

1.41.s:
tasya madhye sabhā ramyā nānākanakamaṇḍitā.
vipulā nāma vikhyātā vipulastambhatoraṇā .. 41.5 ..
1.41.d:
तस्य मध्ये सभा रम्या नानाकनकमण्डिता।
विपुला नाम विख्याता विपुलस्तम्भतोरणा ॥ 41.5 ॥
1.41.m: In its center is a delightful assembly hall decorated with various kinds of gold, / renowned as Vipulā, having expansive pillars and archways.

1.41.s:
tatra tatpuṣpakaṃ nāma nānāratnavibhūṣitam.
mahāvimānaṃ ruciraṃ sarvakāmaguṇairyutam .. 41.6 ..
1.41.d:
तत्र तत्पुष्पकं नाम नानारत्नविभूषितम्।
महाविमानं रुचिरं सर्वकामगुणैर्युतम् ॥ 41.6 ॥
1.41.m: There stands the great aerial car named Puṣpaka, adorned with various jewels, / radiant, endowed with all desirable qualities,

1.41.s:
manojavaṃ kāmagamaṃ hemajālavibhūṣitam.
vāhanaṃ yakṣarājasya kuberasya mahātmanaḥ .. 41.7 ..
1.41.d:
मनोजवं कामगमं हेमजालविभूषितम्।
वाहनं यक्षराजस्य कुबेरस्य महात्मनः ॥ 41.7 ॥
1.41.m: swift as thought, moving at will, decorated with nets of gold, / the vehicle of the king of yakṣas, the great-souled Kubera.

1.41.s:
tatraikapiṅgalo devo mahādevasakhaḥ svayam.
vasati sma sa yakṣendraḥ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtaḥ .. 41.8 ..
1.41.d:
तत्रैकपिङ्गलो देवो महादेवसखः स्वयम्।
वसति स्म स यक्षेन्द्रः सर्वभूतनमस्कृतः ॥ 41.8 ॥
1.41.m: There the god Ekapiṅgala, himself the friend of Mahādeva, / that lord of yakṣas, lived, bowed down to by all beings.

1.41.s:
tatrāpsarogaṇairyyakṣairgandharvaiḥ siddhacāraṇaiḥ.
vasati sma mahātmā'sau kubero devasattamaḥ .. 41.9 ..
1.41.d:
तत्राप्सरोगणैर्य्यक्षैर्गन्धर्वैः सिद्धचारणैः।
वसति स्म महात्माऽसौ कुबेरो देवसत्तमः ॥ 41.9 ॥
1.41.m: There with troops of apsarases, yakṣas, gandharvas, siddhas, and cāraṇas, / lived that great-souled Kubera, foremost among gods.

1.41.s:
tatra padmamahāpadmau tathā makarakacchapau.
kumudaḥ śaṅkha nīlau ca nandano nidhisattamaḥ .. 41.10 ..
1.41.d:
तत्र पद्ममहापद्मौ तथा मकरकच्छपौ।
कुमुदः शङ्ख नीलौ च नन्दनो निधिसत्तमः ॥ 41.10 ॥
1.41.m: There are Padma and Mahāpadma, as well as Makara and Kacchapa, / Kumuda, Śaṅkha, and Nīla, and Nandana, the foremost of treasures.

1.41.s:
aṣṭāvete'kṣayā divyā dhaneśasya mahātmanaḥ.
mahānidhānāstiṣṭhanti sabhāyāṃ ratnasañcitāḥ .. 41.11 ..
1.41.d:
अष्टावेतेऽक्षया दिव्या धनेशस्य महात्मनः।
महानिधानास्तिष्ठन्ति सभायां रत्नसञ्चिताः ॥ 41.11 ॥
1.41.m: These eight imperishable, divine, great treasures of the great-souled lord of wealth, / filled with gems, abide in the assembly hall.

1.41.s:
tathendrāgniyamādīnāṃ devānāmapsarogaṇaiḥ.
teṣāṃ kailāsa āvāso yatra yakṣeśvaraḥ prabhuḥ .. 41.12 ..
1.41.d:
तथेन्द्राग्नियमादीनां देवानामप्सरोगणैः।
तेषां कैलास आवासो यत्र यक्षेश्वरः प्रभुः ॥ 41.12 ॥
1.41.m: Likewise, of the gods Indra, Agni, Yama, and the others, accompanied by groups of apsarases, / the dwelling is Kailāsa, where the lord is the sovereign of yakṣas.

1.41.s:
kṛtvā pūrvamupasthānaṃ yakṣendrasya mahātmanaḥ.
paścādgacchanti ye yasya vihitāḥ paricārakāḥ .. 41.13 ..
1.41.d:
कृत्वा पूर्वमुपस्थानं यक्षेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः।
पश्चाद्गच्छन्ति ये यस्य विहिताः परिचारकाः ॥ 41.13 ॥
1.41.m: Having first paid attendance upon the great-souled lord of yakṣas, / those appointed as attendants subsequently depart, each to his own master.

1.41.s:
tatra mandākinī nāma suramyā vipulodakā.
suvarṇamaṇisopānā nānāpuṣpotkaṭotkaṭā .. 41.14 ..
1.41.d:
तत्र मन्दाकिनी नाम सुरम्या विपुलोदका।
सुवर्णमणिसोपाना नानापुष्पोत्कटोत्कटा ॥ 41.14 ॥
1.41.m: There the Mandākinī, delightful with vast waters, / has steps of gold and gems and is laden with various flowers,

1.41.s:
jāmbūnadamayaiḥ padmairgandhasparśaguṇānvitaiḥ.
nīlavaidūryyapatraiśca gandhopaitairmahotpalaiḥ .. 41.15 ..
1.41.d:
जाम्बूनदमयैः पद्मैर्गन्धस्पर्शगुणान्वितैः।
नीलवैदूर्य्यपत्रैश्च गन्धोपैतैर्महोत्पलैः ॥ 41.15 ॥
1.41.m: with lotuses made of Jāmbūnada gold endowed with fragrance and pleasant touch, / and great water lilies accompanied by fragrance, with petals of blue cat's-eye gems.

1.41.s:
tathā kumudakhaṇḍaiśca mahāpadmairalaṅkṛtā .
yakṣagandharvanārībhirapsarobhiśca śobhitā .. 41.16 ..
1.41.d:
तथा कुमुदखण्डैश्च महापद्मैरलङ्कृता ।
यक्षगन्धर्वनारीभिरप्सरोभिश्च शोभिता ॥ 41.16 ॥
1.41.m: Adorned with beds of white water lilies and great lotuses, / it is graced by yakṣa women, gandharva women, and apsarases.

1.41.s:
devadānavagandharvairyakṣarākṣasapannagaiḥ.
upaspṛṣṭajalā ramyā vāpī mandākinī tathā .. 41.17 ..
1.41.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वैर्यक्षराक्षसपन्नगैः।
उपस्पृष्टजला रम्या वापी मन्दाकिनी तथा ॥ 41.17 ॥
1.41.m: Its waters touched by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, / yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pannagas, such is the lovely Mandākinī pool.

1.41.s:
tathā alakanandā ca nandā ca saritāṃ varā .
etaireva guṇairyuktā nadyo devarṣisevitāḥ .. 41.18 ..
1.41.d:
तथा अलकनन्दा च नन्दा च सरितां वरा ।
एतैरेव गुणैर्युक्ता नद्यो देवर्षिसेविताः ॥ 41.18 ॥
1.41.m: Likewise the Alakanandā, and the Nandā, the best of rivers; / endowed with these very qualities, these rivers are frequented by divine seers.

1.41.s:
tasyaiva śailarājasya pūrve kūṭe pariśrutāḥ.
sahasrayojanāyāmāstriṃśadyojana vistarāḥ .. 41.19 ..
1.41.d:
तस्यैव शैलराजस्य पूर्वे कूटे परिश्रुताः।
सहस्रयोजनायामास्त्रिंशद्योजन विस्तराः ॥ 41.19 ॥
1.41.m: On the eastern ridge of that very king of mountains are renowned / [cities] a thousand yojanas in length and thirty yojanas in breadth,

1.41.s:
daśa gandharvanagarāḥ samṛddhyā parayā yutāḥ.
mahābhavanamālābhiranekābhirvibhūṣitāḥ .. 41.20 ..
1.41.d:
दश गन्धर्वनगराः समृद्ध्या परया युताः।
महाभवनमालाभिरनेकाभिर्विभूषिताः ॥ 41.20 ॥
1.41.m: ten cities of gandharvas, endowed with supreme prosperity, / adorned with numerous rows of great mansions.

1.41.s:
subāhuharikeśādyā ścitrasenajarādayaḥ.
daśa gandharvarājāno dīptavahniparākramāḥ .. 41.21 ..
1.41.d:
सुबाहुहरिकेशाद्या श्चित्रसेनजरादयः।
दश गन्धर्वराजानो दीप्तवह्निपराक्रमाः ॥ 41.21 ॥
1.41.m: Subāhu, Harikeśa, Citrasena, Jarā, and others— / ten gandharva kings possessing prowess like blazing fire [rule there].

1.41.s:
tasyaiva paścime kūṭe kundendusadṛśaprabhe.
nānādhātuśataiścitraiḥ siddha devarṣisevite .. 41.22 ..
1.41.d:
तस्यैव पश्चिमे कूटे कुन्देन्दुसदृशप्रभे।
नानाधातुशतैश्चित्रैः सिद्ध देवर्षिसेविते ॥ 41.22 ॥
1.41.m: On the western ridge of that same [mountain], shining like kunda flowers and the moon, / rich with hundreds of colorful minerals, frequented by siddhas and divine seers,

1.41.s:
aśītiyojanāyāmaṃ catvāriṃśatpravistaram.
ekaikayakṣabhavanaṃ mahābhavanamālinam .. 41.23 ..
1.41.d:
अशीतियोजनायामं चत्वारिंशत्प्रविस्तरम्।
एकैकयक्षभवनं महाभवनमालिनम् ॥ 41.23 ॥
1.41.m: eighty yojanas in length and forty in breadth / is each yakṣa mansion, flanked by rows of great dwellings.

1.41.s:
mahāyakṣālayānyatra triṃśadāḍhyāni me śrṛṇu.
mudā'tha paramaddharyā ca saṃyuktāni samantataḥ .. 41.24 ..
1.41.d:
महायक्षालयान्यत्र त्रिंशदाढ्यानि मे श्रृणु।
मुदाऽथ परमद्धर्या च संयुक्तानि समन्ततः ॥ 41.24 ॥
1.41.m: Hear from me of the thirty rich abodes of great yakṣas there, / filled all around with joy and supreme prosperity.

1.41.s:
mahāmālisunetrādyāstathā maṇivarādayaḥ.
udīrṇā yakṣarājānastatra triṃśatsadā babhuḥ .. 41.25 ..
1.41.d:
महामालिसुनेत्राद्यास्तथा मणिवरादयः।
उदीर्णा यक्षराजानस्तत्र त्रिंशत्सदा बभुः ॥ 41.25 ॥
1.41.m: Mahāmālin, Sunetra, and others, as well as Maṇivara and the rest— / thirty mighty yakṣa kings ever shone there.

1.41.s:
ityete kathitā yakṣā vāyvagnisamatejasaḥ.
yeṣāmadhipatirdevaḥ śrīmān vaiśravaṇaḥ prabhuḥ .. 41.26 ..
1.41.d:
इत्येते कथिता यक्षा वाय्वग्निसमतेजसः।
येषामधिपतिर्देवः श्रीमान् वैश्रवणः प्रभुः ॥ 41.26 ॥
1.41.m: Thus are related these yakṣas, whose splendor equals wind and fire, / whose master is the glorious god, the sovereign Vaiśravaṇa.

1.41.s:
tasyaiva dakṣiṇe pārśve himavatyacalottame.
nikuñjanirjharaguhānaikasānudarītaṭe .. 41.27 ..
1.41.d:
तस्यैव दक्षिणे पार्श्वे हिमवत्यचलोत्तमे।
निकुञ्जनिर्झरगुहानैकसानुदरीतटे ॥ 41.27 ॥
1.41.m: On the southern flank of that very Himavat, the foremost of mountains, / on the slopes of its groves, waterfalls, caves, multiple summits, and chasms,

1.41.s:
arṇavādarṇavaṃ yāvat pūrvapaścāyate'cale.
kinnarāṇāṃ puraśataṃ niviṣṭaṃ vai vkacit vkacit .. 41.28 ..
1.41.d:
अर्णवादर्णवं यावत् पूर्वपश्चायतेऽचले।
किन्नराणां पुरशतं निविष्टं वै व्कचित् व्कचित् ॥ 41.28 ॥
1.41.m: on that mountain extending from ocean to ocean from east to west, / a hundred cities of the kinnaras are established here and there.

1.41.s:
naikaśrṛṅgakalāpasya śailarājasya kukṣiṣu.
naranārīpramuditaṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākulam .. 41.29 ..
1.41.d:
नैकश्रृङ्गकलापस्य शैलराजस्य कुक्षिषु।
नरनारीप्रमुदितं हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलम् ॥ 41.29 ॥
1.41.m: In the interior of the king of mountains, possessing manifold crests, / [the cities] rejoice with men and women, crowded with joyful and flourishing people.

1.41.s:
drumasugrīvasainyādyā bhagadattapuraḥsarāḥ .
yatra rājaśataṃ teṣāṃ dīptānāṃ balaśālinām .. 41.30 ..
1.41.d:
द्रुमसुग्रीवसैन्याद्या भगदत्तपुरःसराः ।
यत्र राजशतं तेषां दीप्तानां बलशालिनाम् ॥ 41.30 ॥
1.41.m: Druma, Sugrīva, Sainyo, and others, led by Bhagadatta— / where [reign] a hundred kings of those [kinnaras], radiant and powerful.

1.41.s:
vivāho yatra rudrasya mahādevyomayā saha.
tapastaptavatī caiva yatra devī varāṅganā .. 41.31 ..
1.41.d:
विवाहो यत्र रुद्रस्य महादेव्योमया सह।
तपस्तप्तवती चैव यत्र देवी वराङ्गना ॥ 41.31 ॥
1.41.m: There took place the marriage of Rudra with the great goddess Umā; / and there the goddess, the excellent woman, performed austerities.

1.41.s:
kirātarūpiṇā caiva yatra rudreṇa krīḍitam.
yatra caiva kṛtaṃ tābhyāṃ jambūdvīpāvalokanam .. 41.32 ..
1.41.d:
किरातरूपिणा चैव यत्र रुद्रेण क्रीडितम्।
यत्र चैव कृतं ताभ्यां जम्बूद्वीपावलोकनम् ॥ 41.32 ॥
1.41.m: And there Rudra, disguised as a Kirāta, engaged in sport; / and there the two cast their gaze upon Jambūdvīpa.

1.41.s:
yatra tāḥ sammudā yuktā nānābhūtagaṇairyutāḥ.
citrapuṣpaphalopetā rudrasyākrīḍabhūmayaḥ .. 41.33 ..
1.41.d:
यत्र ताः सम्मुदा युक्ता नानाभूतगणैर्युताः।
चित्रपुष्पफलोपेता रुद्रस्याक्रीडभूमयः ॥ 41.33 ॥
1.41.m: Where those sporting grounds of Rudra, filled with delight, / accompanied by various groups of bhūtas, abound in colorful flowers and fruits.

1.41.s:
hṛṣṭā giridarīvāsāḥ kṛśodaryyo manoramāḥ.
kundaryo yatra kinnaryyo ramante sma sulocanāḥ .. 41.34 ..
1.41.d:
हृष्टा गिरिदरीवासाः कृशोदर्य्यो मनोरमाः।
कुन्दर्यो यत्र किन्नर्य्यो रमन्ते स्म सुलोचनाः ॥ 41.34 ॥
1.41.m: Joyful, dwelling in mountain caves, slender-waisted and enchanting, / the fair-eyed kinnarī women sport there like kunda blossoms.

1.41.s:
viśālākṣāstathā yakṣā anyāścāpsarasāṅgaṇāḥ.
gandharvāścāṅgaśālinyo yatra tatra mudā yutāḥ .. 41.35 ..
1.41.d:
विशालाक्षास्तथा यक्षा अन्याश्चाप्सरसाङ्गणाः।
गन्धर्वाश्चाङ्गशालिन्यो यत्र तत्र मुदा युताः ॥ 41.35 ॥
1.41.m: Large-eyed yakṣas, other groups of apsarases, / and graceful gandharvas are there filled with joy.

1.41.s:
tatraivomāvanaṃ nāma sarvalokeṣu viśrutam.
ardhanārīnaraṃ rupaṃ dhṛtavān yatra śaṃkaraḥ .. 41.36 ..
1.41.d:
तत्रैवोमावनं नाम सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतम्।
अर्धनारीनरं रुपं धृतवान् यत्र शंकरः ॥ 41.36 ॥
1.41.m: Right there is the forest named Umāvana, renowned in all the worlds, / where Śaṃkara assumed the form of half-woman and half-man.

1.41.s:
tathā śaravaṇaṃ nāma yatra jātaḥ ṣaḍānanaḥ .
yatra caiva kṛtotsāhaḥ krauñcaśailavanaṃ prati .. 41.37 ..
1.41.d:
तथा शरवणं नाम यत्र जातः षडाननः ।
यत्र चैव कृतोत्साहः क्रौञ्चशैलवनं प्रति ॥ 41.37 ॥
1.41.m: Likewise the reed thicket named Śaravaṇa, where the six-faced one was born, / and where he exerted his vigor against the forest of Mount Krauñca.

1.41.s:
dhvajāpatākinañcaiva kiṅkiṇījālamālinam.
yatra siṃharathaṃ yuktaṃ kārtikeyasya dhīmataḥ .. 41.38 ..
1.41.d:
ध्वजापताकिनञ्चैव किङ्किणीजालमालिनम्।
यत्र सिंहरथं युक्तं कार्तिकेयस्य धीमतः ॥ 41.38 ॥
1.41.m: Where, furnished with banners and pennants, garlanded with networks of tiny bells, / is the lion-yoked chariot of the wise Kārttikeya.

1.41.s:
citrapuṣpanikuñjasya krauñcasya ca girestaṭe.
devāriskandanaḥ skando yatra śaktiṃ vimuktavān .. 41.39 ..
1.41.d:
चित्रपुष्पनिकुञ्जस्य क्रौञ्चस्य च गिरेस्तटे।
देवारिस्कन्दनः स्कन्दो यत्र शक्तिं विमुक्तवान् ॥ 41.39 ॥
1.41.m: On the slopes of Mount Krauñca, which has bowers of wonderful flowers, / Skanda, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods, unleashed his spear.

1.41.s:
yatrābhiṣiktaśca guhaḥ sendropendraiḥ surottamaiḥ.
senāpatye ca daityārirdvādaśārkapratāpavān .. 41.40 ..
1.41.d:
यत्राभिषिक्तश्च गुहः सेन्द्रोपेन्द्रैः सुरोत्तमैः।
सेनापत्ये च दैत्यारिर्द्वादशार्कप्रतापवान् ॥ 41.40 ॥
1.41.m: And where Guha, the foe of the daityas possessing the splendor of twelve suns, / was consecrated into generalship by the foremost gods headed by Indra and Upendra.

1.41.s:
bhūtasaṅghāvakīrṇāni etānyanyāni ca dvijāḥ.
tatra tatra kumārasya sthānānyāyatanāni ca .. 41.41 ..
1.41.d:
भूतसङ्घावकीर्णानि एतान्यन्यानि च द्विजाः।
तत्र तत्र कुमारस्य स्थानान्यायतनानि च ॥ 41.41 ॥
1.41.m: Crowded with hosts of bhūtas, these and other / stations and sanctuaries of Kumāra are found here and there, O twice-born.

1.41.s:
tathā pāṇḍuśilā nāma hyākrīḍā krauñcaghātinaḥ.
nānābhūtagaṇākīrṇe pṛṣṭhe himavataḥ śubhe .. 41.42 ..
1.41.d:
तथा पाण्डुशिला नाम ह्याक्रीडा क्रौञ्चघातिनः।
नानाभूतगणाकीर्णे पृष्ठे हिमवतः शुभे ॥ 41.42 ॥
1.41.m: Likewise the sporting ground of the slayer of Krauñca named Pāṇḍuśilā, / on the auspicious back of the Himavat crowded with various groups of bhūtas.

1.41.s:
tasya pūrve taṭe ramye siddhāvāsamudāhṛtam.
kalāpagrāmamityevaṃ nāmnā khyātaṃ manīṣibhiḥ .. 41.43 ..
1.41.d:
तस्य पूर्वे तटे रम्ये सिद्धावासमुदाहृतम्।
कलापग्राममित्येवं नाम्ना ख्यातं मनीषिभिः ॥ 41.43 ॥
1.41.m: On its delightful eastern ridge is declared the abode of the siddhas, / renowned by the wise under the name Kalāpagrāma.

1.41.s:
mṛkaṇḍasya vasiṣṭhasya bharatasya nalasya ca.
viśvāmitrasya viprarṣestathaivoddālakasya ca .. 41.44 ..
1.41.d:
मृकण्डस्य वसिष्ठस्य भरतस्य नलस्य च।
विश्वामित्रस्य विप्रर्षेस्तथैवोद्दालकस्य च ॥ 41.44 ॥
1.41.m:
[The hermitages] of Mṛkaṇḍa, Vasiṣṭha, Bharata, and Nala,
as well as of Viśvāmitra, the priestly seer, and likewise of Uddālaka,

1.41.s:
anyeṣāñcogratapasāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām.
himavatyāśramāṇāñca sahasrāṇi śatāni ca .. 41.45 ..
1.41.d:
अन्येषाञ्चोग्रतपसामृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्।
हिमवत्याश्रमाणाञ्च सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥ 41.45 ॥
1.41.m:
and of other seers of fierce austerities whose minds are purified;
hundreds and thousands of hermitages are on the Himavat,

1.41.s:
naikasidhdagaṇāvāsaṃ sthānāyatanamaṇḍitam.
yakṣagandharvacaritaṃ nānāmlecchagaṇairyutam .. 41.46 ..
1.41.d:
नैकसिध्दगणावासं स्थानायतनमण्डितम्।
यक्षगन्धर्वचरितं नानाम्लेच्छगणैर्युतम् ॥ 41.46 ॥
1.41.m:
an abode of many hosts of siddhas, adorned with shrines and sanctuaries,
frequented by yakṣas and gandharvas, filled with various hosts of Mlecchas,

1.41.s:
nānāratnākarāpūrṇaṃ nānāsattvaniṣevitam.
nānānadīsahasrāṇāṃ sambhavaṃ varaparvatam .. 41.47 ..
1.41.d:
नानारत्नाकरापूर्णं नानासत्त्वनिषेवितम्।
नानानदीसहस्राणां सम्भवं वरपर्वतम् ॥ 41.47 ॥
1.41.m:
filled with mines of various gems, frequented by diverse creatures,
the source of thousands of rivers—an excellent mountain.

1.41.s:
paścimasyācalendrasya niṣadhasya yathārthavat.
kīrttyamānamaśeṣeṇa viśeṣaṃ śrṛṇuta dvijāḥ .. 41.48 ..
1.41.d:
पश्चिमस्याचलेन्द्रस्य निषधस्य यथार्थवत्।
कीर्त्त्यमानमशेषेण विशेषं श्रृणुत द्विजाः ॥ 41.48 ॥
1.41.m:
O twice-born ones, hear now completely and accurately
the distinctive characteristics of the western lord of mountains, Niṣadha, as they are recounted:

1.41.s:
vistīrṇe madhyame kūṭe hemadhā tuvibūṣite.
dīptamāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ siddharṣigaṇasevitam.
yakṣāpsaraḥsamākīrṇaṃ gandharvagaṇasevitam .. 41.49 ..
1.41.d:
विस्तीर्णे मध्यमे कूटे हेमधा तुविबूषिते।
दीप्तमायतनं विष्णोः सिद्धर्षिगणसेवितम्।
यक्षाप्सरःसमाकीर्णं गन्धर्वगणसेवितम् ॥ 41.49 ॥
1.41.m:
On its broad central peak, adorned with golden minerals,
stands the radiant sanctuary of Viṣṇu, frequented by hosts of siddhas and seers,
crowded with yakṣas and apsarases, and served by hosts of gandharvas.

1.41.s:
tatra sākṣānmahādevaḥ pītāmbaradharo hariḥ.
varadaḥ sevyate sirddhairlokakarttā sanātanaḥ .. 41.50 ..
1.41.d:
तत्र साक्षान्महादेवः पीताम्बरधरो हरिः।
वरदः सेव्यते सिर्द्धैर्लोककर्त्ता सनातनः ॥ 41.50 ॥
1.41.m:
There Hari himself, the great god clad in yellow garments,
the giver of boons, the eternal maker of the worlds, is attended upon by the siddhas.

1.41.s:
tasyaivābyantare kūṭe nānādhātuvibhūṣite.
taṭe niṣadhakūṭasya ślakṣṇacāruśilātale .. 41.51 ..
1.41.d:
तस्यैवाब्यन्तरे कूटे नानाधातुविभूषिते।
तटे निषधकूटस्य श्लक्ष्णचारुशिलातले ॥ 41.51 ॥
1.41.m:
On an inner peak of that very mountain, adorned with various minerals,
upon the slope of the peak of Niṣadha, on a smooth and lovely stone surface,

1.41.s:
rukmakāñcananiryūhaṃ taptakāñcanatoraṇam.
anekavalabhīkūṭapralolīśatasaṅkaṭam .. 41.52 ..
1.41.d:
रुक्मकाञ्चननिर्यूहं तप्तकाञ्चनतोरणम्।
अनेकवलभीकूटप्रलोलीशतसङ्कटम् ॥ 41.52 ॥
1.41.m:
stands [a city] with cornices of gold and precious metal, with archways of refined gold,
crowded with hundreds of continuous rows of numerous upper rooms and pinnacles,

1.41.s:
harmyaprāsādamatulaṃ taptakāñcanabhūṣitam.
harmyaprāsādabaddhañca muditañcātivistaram .. 41.53 ..
1.41.d:
हर्म्यप्रासादमतुलं तप्तकाञ्चनभूषितम्।
हर्म्यप्रासादबद्धञ्च मुदितञ्चातिविस्तरम् ॥ 41.53 ॥
1.41.m:
having incomparable mansions and palaces adorned with refined gold,
constructed with mansions and palaces, joyful and of immense extent,

1.41.s:
udyānamālākalitaṃ triṃśadyojanamāyatam.
duḥprasahyamamitraistat pūrṇamāśīviṣopamaiḥ.
ulaṅghīnāṃ pramuditaṃ rakṣasāṃ rākṣasaṃ puram .. 41.54 ..
1.41.d:
उद्यानमालाकलितं त्रिंशद्योजनमायतम्।
दुःप्रसह्यममित्रैस्तत् पूर्णमाशीविषोपमैः।
उलङ्घीनां प्रमुदितं रक्षसां राक्षसं पुरम् ॥ 41.54 ॥
1.41.m:
surrounded by a circle of gardens, thirty yojanas in length,
unbearable to enemies, filled with [beings] resembling venomous serpents:
the joyous rākṣasa city of the encroaching rākṣasas.

1.41.s:
tasyaiva dakṣiṇe pārśve naikadaityagaṇālaye.
guhāpraveśaṃ nagaraṃ śailakukṣau durāsadam .. 41.55 ..
1.41.d:
तस्यैव दक्षिणे पार्श्वे नैकदैत्यगणालये।
गुहाप्रवेशं नगरं शैलकुक्षौ दुरासदम् ॥ 41.55 ॥
1.41.m:
On its southern side, in the abode of many hosts of daityas,
there is a city difficult to approach, situated within a cave in the belly of the mountain.

1.41.s:
tathaiva paścime kūṭe pārijātaśiloccaye.
devadānavabhāgānāṃ samṛddhāni purāṇi tu .. 41.56 ..
1.41.d:
तथैव पश्चिमे कूटे पारिजातशिलोच्चये।
देवदानवभागानां समृद्धानि पुराणि तु ॥ 41.56 ॥
1.41.m:
Likewise on the western peak, on the mountain of the Pārijāta tree,
are the prosperous cities belonging to the portions of the gods and dānavas.

1.41.s:
tatra somaśilā nāma girestasya mahātaṭe.
somo yatrāvatarati sadā parvasu parvasu .. 41.57 ..
1.41.d:
तत्र सोमशिला नाम गिरेस्तस्य महातटे।
सोमो यत्रावतरति सदा पर्वसु पर्वसु ॥ 41.57 ॥
1.41.m:
There, on a great slope of that mountain, is a rock named Somaśilā,
where Soma regularly descends at every node of the lunar month.

1.41.s:
upāsate'tra śrīmantaṃ tārā patimaninditam.
ṛṣikinnaragandharvāḥ sākṣāddevaṃ tamonudam .. 41.58 ..
1.41.d:
उपासतेऽत्र श्रीमन्तं तारा पतिमनिन्दितम्।
ऋषिकिन्नरगन्धर्वाः साक्षाद्देवं तमोनुदम् ॥ 41.58 ॥
1.41.m:
There seers, kinnaras, and gandharvas attend upon
the glorious, faultless lord of Tārā, the visible god who dispels darkness.

1.41.s:
tatraiva cottare kūṭe brahmapārśvamiti smṛtam.
sthānaṃ tatra sureśasya brahmaṇaḥ prathitaṃ divi .. 41.59 ..
1.41.d:
तत्रैव चोत्तरे कूटे ब्रह्मपार्श्वमिति स्मृतम्।
स्थानं तत्र सुरेशस्य ब्रह्मणः प्रथितं दिवि ॥ 41.59 ॥
1.41.m:
On the northern peak of that same mountain is the place known as Brahmapārśva;
the renowned abode of Brahmā, the lord of the gods, is there in heaven.

1.41.s:
ijyāpūjānamaskāraistatra siddhāḥ svayambhuvam.
upāsate mahātmānaṃ yakṣagandharvadānavāḥ .. 41.60 ..
1.41.d:
इज्यापूजानमस्कारैस्तत्र सिद्धाः स्वयम्भुवम्।
उपासते महात्मानं यक्षगन्धर्वदानवाः ॥ 41.60 ॥
1.41.m:
There the siddhas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and dānavas worship
the magnanimous Svayambhū with sacrifices, offerings, and salutations.

1.41.s:
tathaivāyatanaṃ vahneḥ sarvalokeṣu viśrutam.
tatra vigrahavān vāhniḥ sevyate siddhacāraṇaiḥ .. 41.61 ..
1.41.d:
तथैवायतनं वह्नेः सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतम्।
तत्र विग्रहवान् वाह्निः सेव्यते सिद्धचारणैः ॥ 41.61 ॥
1.41.m:
Likewise there is the sanctuary of the Fire-god, renowned throughout all the worlds;
there the Fire-god in bodily form is attended upon by siddhas and cāraṇas.

1.41.s:
tathaiva cottare ramye triśrṛṅge varaparvate.
ṛṣisiddhānucarite nānābhūtagaṇālaye.
puraṃ tat triṣu lokeṣu hemacitrantu viśrutam .. 41.62 ..
1.41.d:
तथैव चोत्तरे रम्ये त्रिश्रृङ्गे वरपर्वते।
ऋषिसिद्धानुचरिते नानाभूतगणालये।
पुरं तत् त्रिषु लोकेषु हेमचित्रन्तु विश्रुतम् ॥ 41.62 ॥
1.41.m:
Likewise in the north, on the lovely, excellent mountain Triśṛṅga,
frequented by seers and siddhas, the abode of diverse hosts of bhūtas,
is a city famous throughout the three worlds, wondrous with gold.

1.41.s:
trayāṇāṃ devamukhyānāṃ trīṇyevāyatanāni ca.
nārāyaṇasyāyatanaṃ pūrvakūṭe dvijottamāḥ .
madhyame brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ śaṅkarasya tu paścime .. 41.63 ..
1.41.d:
त्रयाणां देवमुख्यानां त्रीण्येवायतनानि च।
नारायणस्यायतनं पूर्वकूटे द्विजोत्तमाः ।
मध्यमे ब्रह्मणः स्थानं शङ्करस्य तु पश्चिमे ॥ 41.63 ॥
1.41.m:
There are three sanctuaries of the three chief gods:
O best of the twice-born, the sanctuary of Nārāyaṇa is on the eastern peak,
the abode of Brahmā is on the middle [peak], and that of Śaṅkara is on the western.

1.41.s:
daityadānavagandharvairyakṣarākṣasapannagaiḥ.
ijānā abhipūjyante devadevā mahābalāḥ .. 41.64 ..
1.41.d:
दैत्यदानवगन्धर्वैर्यक्षराक्षसपन्नगैः।
इजाना अभिपूज्यन्ते देवदेवा महाबलाः ॥ 41.64 ॥
1.41.m:
Performing sacrifices, daityas, dānavas, gandharvas,
yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pannagas worship those mighty gods of gods.

1.41.s:
tathā purāṇi ramyāṇi deśe caiva vkacit vkacit.
yakṣagandharvanāgānāṃ triśrṛṅge varaparvate .. 41.65 ..
1.41.d:
तथा पुराणि रम्याणि देशे चैव व्कचित् व्कचित्।
यक्षगन्धर्वनागानां त्रिश्रृङ्गे वरपर्वते ॥ 41.65 ॥
1.41.m:
Likewise, delightful cities of yakṣas, gandharvas, and nāgas
are located here and there on the excellent mountain Triśṛṅga.

1.41.s:
tathaiva cottare deśe cārudhau devaparvate.
anekaśrṛṅgakalite siddhasādhu niṣevite .. 41.66 ..
1.41.d:
तथैव चोत्तरे देशे चारुधौ देवपर्वते।
अनेकश्रृङ्गकलिते सिद्धसाधु निषेविते ॥ 41.66 ॥
1.41.m:
Likewise in the northern region, on the beautiful divine mountain [Triśṛṅga],
endowed with numerous peaks, frequented by siddhas and holy ascetics,

1.41.s:
yakṣāṇāṃ kinnarāṇāñca gandharvāṇāṃ sahasraśaḥ.
nāgānāṃ rākṣasānāñca daityānāñca mahābale .. 41.67 ..
1.41.d:
यक्षाणां किन्नराणाञ्च गन्धर्वाणां सहस्रशः।
नागानां राक्षसानाञ्च दैत्यानाञ्च महाबले ॥ 41.67 ॥
1.41.m:
by thousands of yakṣas, kinnaras, and gandharvas,
and by nāgas, rākṣasas, and daityas of great might,

1.41.s:
kūṭe tu madhyame tasya siddhasaṅgha niṣevite.
ramye devarṣicarite ratnadhātuvibhūṣite .. 41.68 ..
1.41.d:
कूटे तु मध्यमे तस्य सिद्धसङ्घ निषेविते।
रम्ये देवर्षिचरिते रत्नधातुविभूषिते ॥ 41.68 ॥
1.41.m:
on its central peak, frequented by assemblies of siddhas,
charming, trodden by celestial seers, adorned with gems and minerals,

1.41.s:
pajhotpalavanaiḥ phullaiḥ saugandhikavanaistathā.
tathā kumudakhaṇḍaiśca vikacairupaśobhite .. 41.69 ..
1.41.d:
पझोत्पलवनैः फुल्लैः सौगन्धिकवनैस्तथा।
तथा कुमुदखण्डैश्च विकचैरुपशोभिते ॥ 41.69 ॥
1.41.m:
adorned with blooming clusters of lotuses and blue lotuses,
with groves of saugandhika blossoms, and with clusters of opened white water-lilies,

1.41.s:
vihaṅgasaṅghasaṃghuṣṭaṃ nānāsatvaniṣevitam.
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇaṃ mattaṣaṭ‌padasevitam .. 41.70 ..
1.41.d:
विहङ्गसङ्घसंघुष्टं नानासत्वनिषेवितम्।
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं मत्तषट्‌पदसेवितम् ॥ 41.70 ॥
1.41.m:
resounding with flocks of birds, frequented by diverse creatures,
teeming with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, visited by intoxicated bees,

1.41.s:
nānāsatvagaṇākīrṇaṃ vihaṅgairupaśobhitam.
cārutīrthasusambādhaṃ triṃśadyojanamaṇḍalam .. 41.71 ..
1.41.d:
नानासत्वगणाकीर्णं विहङ्गैरुपशोभितम्।
चारुतीर्थसुसम्बाधं त्रिंशद्योजनमण्डलम् ॥ 41.71 ॥
1.41.m:
thronged with hosts of diverse creatures, beautified by birds,
and closely bordered with charming sacred bathing-places, thirty yojanas in circumference,

1.41.s:
siddhairupaspṛṣṭajalaṃ jaladoṣavivarjitam.
tatrānandajalannāma mahāpuṇyajalaṃ saraḥ .. 41.72 ..
1.41.d:
सिद्धैरुपस्पृष्टजलं जलदोषविवर्जितम्।
तत्रानन्दजलन्नाम महापुण्यजलं सरः ॥ 41.72 ॥
1.41.m:
its waters sipped by siddhas, free of any waterborne defect,
is a lake of exceedingly holy water named Ānandajala.

1.41.s:
tatra nāgapati ścaṇḍa ścaṇḍo nāma durāsadaḥ.
śataśīrṣā mahābhāgo viṣṇucakrāṅkacihnitaḥ.
ityevamaṣṭau vijñeyā vicitrā devaparvatāḥ .. 41.73 ...
1.41.d:
तत्र नागपति श्चण्ड श्चण्डो नाम दुरासदः।
शतशीर्षा महाभागो विष्णुचक्राङ्कचिह्नितः।
इत्येवमष्टौ विज्ञेया विचित्रा देवपर्वताः ॥ 41.73 ॥।
1.41.m:
There dwells the fierce lord of nāgas named Caṇḍa, difficult to overcome,
hundred-headed, highly fortunate, marked with the sign of Viṣṇu’s discus.
In this way are the eight wondrous divine mountains to be known,

1.41.s:
purairāyatanaiḥ puṇyaiḥ puṇyodaiśca sarovaraiḥ.
suvarṇaparvatairnaikaistathā rajataparvataiḥ .. 41.74 ..
1.41.d:
पुरैरायतनैः पुण्यैः पुण्योदैश्च सरोवरैः।
सुवर्णपर्वतैर्नैकैस्तथा रजतपर्वतैः ॥ 41.74 ॥
1.41.m:
endowed with cities, holy sanctuaries, and lakes of holy water,
with many mountains of gold and mountains of silver,

1.41.s:
nānāratnaprabhāsaiśca naikaiśca maṇiparvataiḥ.
haritālaparvatairnaikaistathā hiṅgulakāñcanaiḥ .. 41.75 ..
1.41.d:
नानारत्नप्रभासैश्च नैकैश्च मणिपर्वतैः।
हरितालपर्वतैर्नैकैस्तथा हिङ्गुलकाञ्चनैः ॥ 41.75 ॥
1.41.m:
with numerous jewel-mountains shining with various gems,
with many mountains of yellow orpiment, as well as of cinnabar and gold,

1.41.s:
śuddhairmanaḥ śilājālairbhāsvarairaruṇaprabhaiḥ .
nānādhātuvicitraiśca naikaiśca maṇiparvataiḥ .. 41.76 ..
1.41.d:
शुद्धैर्मनः शिलाजालैर्भास्वरैररुणप्रभैः ।
नानाधातुविचित्रैश्च नैकैश्च मणिपर्वतैः ॥ 41.76 ॥
1.41.m:
with masses of pure realgar, radiant with reddish luster,
and with many jewel-mountains variegated with diverse minerals.

1.41.s:
pūrṇā vasumatī sarvā giribhirnaikavistaraiḥ.
nadīkandaraśailādyairanekaiścitrasānubhiḥ .. 41.77 ..
1.41.d:
पूर्णा वसुमती सर्वा गिरिभिर्नैकविस्तरैः।
नदीकन्दरशैलाद्यैरनेकैश्चित्रसानुभिः ॥ 41.77 ॥
1.41.m:
The entire earth is filled with mountains of diverse extents,
with rivers, caves, crags, and the like, and with many wondrous ridges.

1.41.s:
ityevamacalairyuktairdaityarākṣasasādhubhiḥ.
kinnaroragagandharvairvicitraiḥ siddhacāraṇaiḥ .. 41.78 ..
1.41.d:
इत्येवमचलैर्युक्तैर्दैत्यराक्षससाधुभिः।
किन्नरोरगगन्धर्वैर्विचित्रैः सिद्धचारणैः ॥ 41.78 ॥
1.41.m:
Surrounded thus by mountains populated by daityas, rākṣasas, and holy ascetics,
by wondrous kinnaras, uragas, gandharvas, siddhas, and cāraṇas,

1.41.s:
gandharvairapsarobhiśca sevitā naika vistarāḥ.
puṇyakṛdbhiḥ samākīrṇā kesarākṛtayo nagāḥ .. 41.79 ..
1.41.d:
गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च सेविता नैक विस्तराः।
पुण्यकृद्भिः समाकीर्णा केसराकृतयो नगाः ॥ 41.79 ॥
1.41.m:
and frequented by gandharvas and apsarases, of multiple extents,
these mountains, shaped like filaments [of a lotus], are crowded with performers of meritorious deeds.

1.41.s:
girijālantu tanmeroḥ siddhalokamiti smṛtam.
citraṃ nānāśrayopetaṃ pracāraṃ sukṛtātmanām .. 41.80 ..
1.41.d:
गिरिजालन्तु तन्मेरोः सिद्धलोकमिति स्मृतम्।
चित्रं नानाश्रयोपेतं प्रचारं सुकृतात्मनाम् ॥ 41.80 ॥
1.41.m:
That mountain system of Meru is known as the world of the siddhas,
wondrous, provided with various shelters, the resort of people of virtuous deeds.

1.41.s:
nātyugrakarmasiddhānāṃ pratimā madhyamāḥ smṛtāḥ.
sa hi svarga iti khyātaḥ kramastveṣa prakīrtitaḥ .. 41.81 ..
1.41.d:
नात्युग्रकर्मसिद्धानां प्रतिमा मध्यमाः स्मृताः।
स हि स्वर्ग इति ख्यातः क्रमस्त्वेष प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 41.81 ॥
1.41.m:
They are considered intermediate manifestations for those who have accomplished moderately severe deeds;
that indeed is known as heaven, and such is the order proclaimed.

1.41.s: caturmahādvīpavatī seyamurvī prakīrtitā ..
1.41.d: चतुर्महाद्वीपवती सेयमुर्वी प्रकीर्तिता ॥
1.41.m:
This earth is proclaimed as possessing four great continents,
with varied colours and dimensions, and likewise varied castes and strengths.

1.41.s: nānāvarṇapramāṇairhi nānāvarṇabalaistathā .. 41.82 ..
1.41.d: नानावर्णप्रमाणैर्हि नानावर्णबलैस्तथा ॥ 41.82 ॥

1.41.s:
nānābhakṣyānnapānaiśca nānācchādanabhūṣaṇaiḥ.
prajāvikārairvividhaiścitrairadhyuṣitaiḥ saha.. 41.83 ..
1.41.d:
नानाभक्ष्यान्नपानैश्च नानाच्छादनभूषणैः।
प्रजाविकारैर्विविधैश्चित्रैरध्युषितैः सह॥ 41.83 ॥
1.41.m:
together with inhabitants of diverse, wondrous transformations of peoples
characterized by various foods, grains, and drinks, and various garments and ornaments.

1.41.s:
catvāro naikavarṇādyā mahādvīpāḥ pariśrutāḥ.
bhadrāśca bharatāścaiva ketumālāśca paścimāḥ.
uttarāḥ kuravaścaiva kṛtapuṇyapratiśrayāḥ .. 41.84 ..
1.41.d:
चत्वारो नैकवर्णाद्या महाद्वीपाः परिश्रुताः।
भद्राश्च भरताश्चैव केतुमालाश्च पश्चिमाः।
उत्तराः कुरवश्चैव कृतपुण्यप्रतिश्रयाः ॥ 41.84 ॥
1.41.m:
Four great continents distinguished by diverse castes and the like are renowned:
Bhadrāśva, Bhārata, Ketumāla in the west,
and the northern Kurus, the refuge of those who have performed meritorious deeds.

1.41.s:
saiṣā caturmahādvīpā nānādvīpasamākulā.
pṛthivī kīrtitā kṛtsnā padmākārā mayā dvijāḥ .. 41.85 ..
1.41.d:
सैषा चतुर्महाद्वीपा नानाद्वीपसमाकुला।
पृथिवी कीर्तिता कृत्स्ना पद्माकारा मया द्विजाः ॥ 41.85 ॥
1.41.m:
O twice-born ones, this entire earth, having four great continents
and filled with various islands, has thus been described by me in the form of a lotus.

1.41.s:
tadeṣā sāntaradvīpā saśailavanakānanā.
padmetyabhihitā kṛtsnā pṛthivī bahuvistarā .. 41.86 ..
1.41.d:
तदेषा सान्तरद्वीपा सशैलवनकानना।
पद्मेत्यभिहिता कृत्स्ना पृथिवी बहुविस्तरा ॥ 41.86 ॥
1.41.m: Therefore, this entire, vast earth, / with its intermediate continents, mountains, and forests, is called a lotus. 41.86

1.41.s:
sabrahmasadanaṃ lokaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam.
trilokamiti vikhyātaṃ yatsattvairvyavahāryate .. 41.87 ..
1.41.d:
सब्रह्मसदनं लोकं सदेवासुरमानुषम्।
त्रिलोकमिति विख्यातं यत्सत्त्वैर्व्यवहार्यते ॥ 41.87 ॥
1.41.m: Together with Brahmā's abode, the world, with gods, asuras, and human beings, / is renowned as the threefold world, which is inhabited by living beings. 41.87

1.41.s:
candrādityāvataptaṃ yattajjagat parigīyate.
gandhavarṇarasopetaṃ śabdasparśaguṇānvitam .. 41.88 ..
1.41.d:
चन्द्रादित्यावतप्तं यत्तज्जगत् परिगीयते।
गन्धवर्णरसोपेतं शब्दस्पर्शगुणान्वितम् ॥ 41.88 ॥
1.41.m: That which is heated by the moon and sun is proclaimed to be the universe, / endowed with fragrance, color, and taste, and possessed of the qualities of sound and touch. 41.88

1.41.s:
taṃ lokapadmaṃ śrutibhiḥ padmamityabhidhīyate.
eṣa sarvapurāṇeṣu kramaḥ supariniścitaḥ .. 41.89 ..
1.41.d:
तं लोकपद्मं श्रुतिभिः पद्ममित्यभिधीयते।
एष सर्वपुराणेषु क्रमः सुपरिनिश्चितः ॥ 41.89 ॥
1.41.m: That world-lotus is designated as a lotus by the Vedic texts. / This order is well established in all the Purāṇas. 41.89

1.41.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte bhuvanavinyāso nāmaikacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 41 ..
1.41.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते भुवनविन्यासो नामैकचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 41 ॥
1.41.m: Thus ends the forty-first chapter, named 'The Arrangement of the Worlds,' in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu. 41

1.42.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.42.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.42.m:
The Sūta said:
From the lakes have issued holy rivers of the gods
and rivers carrying great torrents of water; listen to them in due order.

1.42.s:
sarovarebhyaḥ puṇyodā deva nadyo vinirgatāḥ.
mahaughatoyā nadyaśca tāḥ śrṛṇudhvaṃ yathākramam .. 42.1 ..
1.42.d:
सरोवरेभ्यः पुण्योदा देव नद्यो विनिर्गताः।
महौघतोया नद्यश्च ताः श्रृणुध्वं यथाक्रमम् ॥ 42.1 ॥

1.42.s:
ākāśāmbhonidheryo'sau soma ityabhidhīyate.
ādhāraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ devānāmamṛtākaraḥ .. 42.2 ..
1.42.d:
आकाशाम्भोनिधेर्योऽसौ सोम इत्यभिधीयते।
आधारः सर्वभूतानां देवानाममृताकरः ॥ 42.2 ॥
1.42.m: That reservoir of water in the sky which is called Soma, / the support of all beings, the mine of nectar for the gods— 42.2

1.42.s:
tasmāt pravṛttā puṇyodā nadī hyākāśagāminī.
saptamenānilapathā prayātā vimalodakā .. 42.3 ..
1.42.d:
तस्मात् प्रवृत्ता पुण्योदा नदी ह्याकाशगामिनी।
सप्तमेनानिलपथा प्रयाता विमलोदका ॥ 42.3 ॥
1.42.m: from it proceeds the river that traverses the sky, with holy waters; / it flows along the seventh wind-path, with pure waters. 42.3

1.42.s:
sā jyotiṣi nivartantī jyotirgaṇaniṣevitā.
tārākojisahasrāṇāṃ nabhasaśca samāyatā .. 42.4 ..
1.42.d:
सा ज्योतिषि निवर्तन्ती ज्योतिर्गणनिषेविता।
ताराकोजिसहस्राणां नभसश्च समायता ॥ 42.4 ॥
1.42.m: Revolving among the heavenly luminaries, attended by hosts of luminaries, / it stretches through thousands of crores of stars and across the sky. 42.4

1.42.s:
māhendreṇa gajendreṇa ākāśapathayāyinā.
krīḍitā hyantaratale yā sā vikṣobhitodakā .. 42.5 ..
1.42.d:
माहेन्द्रेण गजेन्द्रेण आकाशपथयायिना।
क्रीडिता ह्यन्तरतले या सा विक्षोभितोदका ॥ 42.5 ॥
1.42.m: Sported in by Indra's great elephant that travels the path of the sky, / its waters are stirred up in the intermediate space. 42.5

1.42.s:
naikairvimānasaṅghātaiḥ prakrāmadbhirnabhastalam.
siddhairupaspṛṣṭajalā mahāpuṇyajalā śivā .. 42.6 ..
1.42.d:
नैकैर्विमानसङ्घातैः प्रक्रामद्भिर्नभस्तलम्।
सिद्धैरुपस्पृष्टजला महापुण्यजला शिवा ॥ 42.6 ॥
1.42.m: Crossed by numerous hosts of celestial chariots traversing the firmament, / its waters touched by the siddhas, it is auspicious, with waters of great merit. 42.6

1.42.s:
vāyunā preryamāṇā ca anekābhogagāminī.
parivarttatyaharaharyathā sūryastathaiva sā .. 42.7 ..
1.42.d:
वायुना प्रेर्यमाणा च अनेकाभोगगामिनी।
परिवर्त्तत्यहरहर्यथा सूर्यस्तथैव सा ॥ 42.7 ॥
1.42.m: Driven by the wind and flowing through many expanses, / it turns every day just as the sun does. 42.7

1.42.s:
catvāryaśītiḥ pratatā yojanānāṃ samantataḥ.
vegena kurvatī meruṃ sā prayātā pradakṣiṇam .. 42.8 ..
1.42.d:
चत्वार्यशीतिः प्रतता योजनानां समन्ततः।
वेगेन कुर्वती मेरुं सा प्रयाता प्रदक्षिणम् ॥ 42.8 ॥
1.42.m: Extending eighty-four yojanas on all sides, / making a clockwise circuit around Meru with its speed, it advances. 42.8

1.42.s:
vibhidyamānā salilaistaijasenānilena ca.
meroruttarakūṭeṣu patitātha caturṣvapi .. 42.9 ..
1.42.d:
विभिद्यमाना सलिलैस्तैजसेनानिलेन च।
मेरोरुत्तरकूटेषु पतिताथ चतुर्ष्वपि ॥ 42.9 ॥
1.42.m: Divided by its waters and by the fiery wind, / it then fell upon the four northern peaks of Meru. 42.9

1.42.s:
merukūṭataṭāntebhya utkṛṣṭebhyo nivartitā.
vikīryamāṇa salilā caturddhāsaṃsṛtodakā .. 42.10 ..
1.42.d:
मेरुकूटतटान्तेभ्य उत्कृष्टेभ्यो निवर्तिता।
विकीर्यमाण सलिला चतुर्द्धासंसृतोदका ॥ 42.10 ॥
1.42.m: Turned back from the high edges of the peaks of Meru, / its waters scattered, its current flowed forth in four branches. 42.10

1.42.s:
ṣaṣṭiyojanasāhasraṃ nirālambanamambaram.
nipapāta mahābhāga merostasya caturddiśam .. 42.11 ..
1.42.d:
षष्टियोजनसाहस्रं निरालम्बनमम्बरम्।
निपपात महाभाग मेरोस्तस्य चतुर्द्दिशम् ॥ 42.11 ॥
1.42.m: Across sixty thousand yojanas of unsupported sky, / it fell down, O fortunate one, in the four directions of that Meru. 42.11

1.42.s:
sā caturṣvabhitaścaiva mahāpādeṣu śobhanā.
puṇyā mandarapūrveṇa patitā hi mahānadī .. 42.12 ..
1.42.d:
सा चतुर्ष्वभितश्चैव महापादेषु शोभना।
पुण्या मन्दरपूर्वेण पतिता हि महानदी ॥ 42.12 ॥
1.42.m: Beautiful around the four great foot-hills, / that holy great river indeed fell to the east of Mandara. 42.12

1.42.s:
pūrveṇāṃśena devānāṃ sarvasiddhagaṇālayam.
suvarṇacitrakaṭakaṃ naikanirjharakandaram .. 42.13 ..
1.42.d:
पूर्वेणांशेन देवानां सर्वसिद्धगणालयम्।
सुवर्णचित्रकटकं नैकनिर्झरकन्दरम् ॥ 42.13 ॥
1.42.m: With its eastern portion, [reaching the mountain] of the gods, the abode of all hosts of siddhas, / with slopes variegated with gold, and manifold cascades and caves, 42.13

1.42.s:
plāvayantī saśailendraṃ mandarañcārukandaram.
vaprapratāpaśamanairanekaiḥ sphāṭikodakaiḥ .. 42.14 ..
1.42.d:
प्लावयन्ती सशैलेन्द्रं मन्दरञ्चारुकन्दरम्।
वप्रप्रतापशमनैरनेकैः स्फाटिकोदकैः ॥ 42.14 ॥
1.42.m: flooding Mandara, king of mountains, with its beautiful caves, / with its many crystal waters that relieve the heat of its ramparts, 42.14

1.42.s:
tathā caitrarathaṃ ramyaṃ plāvayantī pradakṣiṇam.
praviṣṭā hyambaranadī hyaruṇodasarovaram .. 42.15 ..
1.42.d:
तथा चैत्ररथं रम्यं प्लावयन्ती प्रदक्षिणम्।
प्रविष्टा ह्यम्बरनदी ह्यरुणोदसरोवरम् ॥ 42.15 ॥
1.42.m: and encircling the delightful Caitraratha, flooding it, / the heavenly river entered the Aruṇoda lake. 42.15

1.42.s:
aruṇodānnivṛttā'tha śītānte ramyanirjhare.
śaile siddhagaṇāvāse nipapāta sugāminī .. 42.16 ..
1.42.d:
अरुणोदान्निवृत्ताऽथ शीतान्ते रम्यनिर्झरे।
शैले सिद्धगणावासे निपपात सुगामिनी ॥ 42.16 ॥
1.42.m: Issuing forth from Aruṇoda, flowing gracefully, / it fell upon Mount Śītānta, which has lovely waterfalls and is the dwelling of hosts of siddhas. 42.16

1.42.s:
sītā nāma mahā puṇyā nadīnāṃ pravarā nadī.
sā nikuñjaniruddhā tu anekābhogagāminī .. 42.17 ..
1.42.d:
सीता नाम महा पुण्या नदीनां प्रवरा नदी।
सा निकुञ्जनिरुद्धा तु अनेकाभोगगामिनी ॥ 42.17 ॥
1.42.m: It is the most excellent among rivers, exceedingly holy, named Sītā; / blocked by bowers, yet flowing through many expanses, 42.17

1.42.s:
śītāntāśikharādbhraṣṭā sukuñje varaparvate.
nipapāta mahābhāgā tasmādapi sumañjasam .. 42.18 ..
1.42.d:
शीतान्ताशिखराद्भ्रष्टा सुकुञ्जे वरपर्वते।
निपपात महाभागा तस्मादपि सुमञ्जसम् ॥ 42.18 ॥
1.42.m: and falling from the peak of Śītānta onto the excellent mountain Sukuñja, / that fortunate [river] then moved very straight from there. 42.18

1.42.s:
tasmānmālyavataṃ śailaṃ bhāvayantī varāpagā.
vaikaṅkaṃ samanuprāptā vaikaṅkānmaṇiparvatam.
maṇiparvatānmahāśailaṃ ṛṣabhaṃ naikakandaram .. 42.19 ..
1.42.d:
तस्मान्माल्यवतं शैलं भावयन्ती वरापगा।
वैकङ्कं समनुप्राप्ता वैकङ्कान्मणिपर्वतम्।
मणिपर्वतान्महाशैलं ऋषभं नैककन्दरम् ॥ 42.19 ॥
1.42.m: From there, that best of streams, honoring Mount Mālyavat, / reached Vaikaṅka; from Vaikaṅka to the Maṇi mountain; / from the Maṇi mountain to the great mountain Ṛṣabha, which has many caves. 42.19

1.42.s:
evaṃ śailasahasrāṇi dārayantī mahānadī.
patitā'tha mahāśaile jaṭhare siddhasevite .. 42.20 ..
1.42.d:
एवं शैलसहस्राणि दारयन्ती महानदी।
पतिताऽथ महाशैले जठरे सिद्धसेविते ॥ 42.20 ॥
1.42.m: Thus cleaving thousands of mountains, that great river / then fell upon the great mountain Jaṭhara, frequented by siddhas. 42.20

1.42.s:
tasmādapi mahāśailaṃ devakūṭaṃ taraṅgiṇī.
tasya kukṣisamudrāntā krameṇa pṛthivīṃ gatā .. 42.21 ..
1.42.d:
तस्मादपि महाशैलं देवकूटं तरङ्गिणी।
तस्य कुक्षिसमुद्रान्ता क्रमेण पृथिवीं गता ॥ 42.21 ॥
1.42.m: From there also, that river [flowed] to the great mountain Devakūṭa; / reaching the sea from its belly, it gradually arrived at the earth. 42.21

1.42.s:
saivaṃ sthalīsahasrāṇi śailarājaśatāni ca.
vanāni ca vicitrāṇi sarāṃsi vividhāni ca .. 42.22 ..
1.42.d:
सैवं स्थलीसहस्राणि शैलराजशतानि च।
वनानि च विचित्राणि सरांसि विविधानि च ॥ 42.22 ॥
1.42.m: Thus, across thousands of plateaus and hundreds of kingly mountains, / various forests and diverse lakes, 42.22

1.42.s:
srāvayantī mahābhāgā visphāreṣvavalīkadā.
nadī sahasrānugatā pravṛttā ca mahānadī .. 42.23 ..
1.42.d:
स्रावयन्ती महाभागा विस्फारेष्ववलीकदा।
नदी सहस्रानुगता प्रवृत्ता च महानदी ॥ 42.23 ॥
1.42.m: overflowing on the broad expanses [...], / that fortunate great river, followed by thousands of streams, proceeded. 42.23

1.42.s:
bhadrāśvaṃ sumahādvīpaṃ plāvayantī varāpagā.
praviṣṭā hyarṇavaṃ pūrvaṃ pūrve dvīpe mahānadī .. 42.24 ..
1.42.d:
भद्राश्वं सुमहाद्वीपं प्लावयन्ती वरापगा।
प्रविष्टा ह्यर्णवं पूर्वं पूर्वे द्वीपे महानदी ॥ 42.24 ॥
1.42.m: Flooding the immense continent of Bhadrāśva, that best of streams, / that great river entered the eastern ocean in the eastern continent. 42.24

1.42.s:
dakṣiṇe'pi prapannā yā śailendre gandhamādane.
citraiḥ prapātairvidhairnaikavisphālitodakā .. 42.25 ..
1.42.d:
दक्षिणेऽपि प्रपन्ना या शैलेन्द्रे गन्धमादने।
चित्रैः प्रपातैर्विधैर्नैकविस्फालितोदका ॥ 42.25 ॥
1.42.m: That which descended to the south upon Gandhamādana, king of mountains, / its waters shattered in diverse ways by picturesque waterfalls, 42.25

1.42.s:
tadghandhamādanavanaṃ nandanaṃ devanandanam.
plāvayantī mahābhāgā prayātā sā pradakṣiṇam .. 42.26 ..
1.42.d:
तद्घन्धमादनवनं नन्दनं देवनन्दनम्।
प्लावयन्ती महाभागा प्रयाता सा प्रदक्षिणम् ॥ 42.26 ॥
1.42.m: flooding that Gandhamādana forest, the Nandana that delights the gods, / that fortunate [river] advanced clockwise. 42.26

1.42.s:
nāmnā hyalakanandeti sarvalokeṣu viśrutā.
praviśatyuttarasaro mānasaṃ devamānasam .. 42.27 ..
1.42.d:
नाम्ना ह्यलकनन्देति सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुता।
प्रविशत्युत्तरसरो मानसं देवमानसम् ॥ 42.27 ॥
1.42.m: Known in all the worlds by the name Alakanandā, / it enters the northern lake, Mānasa, the divine Mānasa. 42.27

1.42.s:
mānasācchailarājānaṃ ramyaṃ triśikharaṃ gatā.
trikūṭācchailaśikharāt kaliṅgaśikharaṃ gatā .. 42.28 ..
1.42.d:
मानसाच्छैलराजानं रम्यं त्रिशिखरं गता।
त्रिकूटाच्छैलशिखरात् कलिङ्गशिखरं गता ॥ 42.28 ॥
1.42.m: From Mānasa it went to the delightful Triśikhara, king of mountains; / from the mountain peak Trikūṭa it went to the peak of Kaliṅga. 42.28

1.42.s:
kaliṅgaśikharādbhraṣṭā rucake nipapāta sā.
rucakānniṣadhaṃ prāptā tāmrābhaṃ niṣadhādapi .. 42.29 ..
1.42.d:
कलिङ्गशिखराद्भ्रष्टा रुचके निपपात सा।
रुचकान्निषधं प्राप्ता ताम्राभं निषधादपि ॥ 42.29 ॥
1.42.m: Falling from the peak of Kaliṅga, it dropped onto Rucaka; / from Rucaka it reached Niṣadha, and from Niṣadha to Tāmrābha. 42.29

1.42.s:
tāmrābhaśikharārdbhraṣṭā gatā śvetodaraṃ girim .
tasmātsumūlaṃ śailendraṃ vasudhārañca parvatam .. 42.30 ..
1.42.d:
ताम्राभशिखरार्द्भ्रष्टा गता श्वेतोदरं गिरिम् ।
तस्मात्सुमूलं शैलेन्द्रं वसुधारञ्च पर्वतम् ॥ 42.30 ॥
1.42.m: Falling from the peak of Tāmrābha, it went to Mount Śvetodara; / from there to Sumūla, king of mountains, and to Mount Vasudhāra. 42.30

1.42.s:
hemakūṭaṃ gatā tasmāddevaśrṛṅge tato gatā.
tasmādgatā mahāśailaṃ tataścāpi piśācakam .. 42.31 ..
1.42.d:
हेमकूटं गता तस्माद्देवश्रृङ्गे ततो गता।
तस्माद्गता महाशैलं ततश्चापि पिशाचकम् ॥ 42.31 ॥
1.42.m: From there it went to Hemakūṭa, and then to Devaśṛṅga; / from there to a great mountain, and then to Piśācaka. 42.31

1.42.s:
piśācakācchailavarāt pañcakūṭaṅgatā punaḥ.
pañcakūṭāttu kailāsaṃ devāvāsaṃ śiloccayam .. 42.32 ..
1.42.d:
पिशाचकाच्छैलवरात् पञ्चकूटङ्गता पुनः।
पञ्चकूटात्तु कैलासं देवावासं शिलोच्चयम् ॥ 42.32 ॥
1.42.m: From Piśācaka, best of mountains, it went again to Pañcakūṭa; / and from Pañcakūṭa to Kailāsa, the mountain abode of the gods. 42.32

1.42.s:
tasya kukṣiṣu vibhrāntā naikakandarasānuṣu.
himavatyuttamanadī nipapātācalottame .. 42.33 ..
1.42.d:
तस्य कुक्षिषु विभ्रान्ता नैककन्दरसानुषु।
हिमवत्युत्तमनदी निपपाताचलोत्तमे ॥ 42.33 ॥
1.42.m: Wandering within its recesses, among its many caves and ridges, / that most excellent river fell upon Himavat, best of mountains. 42.33

1.42.s:
saivaṃ śailasahasrāṇi dārayantī mahānadī.
sthalīśatānyanekāni plāvayantyāśugāṇinī .. 42.34 ..
1.42.d:
सैवं शैलसहस्राणि दारयन्ती महानदी।
स्थलीशतान्यनेकानि प्लावयन्त्याशुगाणिनी ॥ 42.34 ॥
1.42.m: Thus cleaving thousands of mountains, that great river, / flowing swiftly, inundating hundreds of diverse plateaus, 42.34

1.42.s:
vanānāñca sahasrāṇi kandarāṇāṃ śatāni ca .
srāvayantī mahābhāgā prayātā dakṣiṇodadhim .. 42.35 ..
1.42.d:
वनानाञ्च सहस्राणि कन्दराणां शतानि च ।
स्रावयन्ती महाभागा प्रयाता दक्षिणोदधिम् ॥ 42.35 ॥
1.42.m: overflowing thousands of forests and hundreds of caves, / that fortunate [river] advanced to the southern ocean. 42.35

1.42.s:
ramyā yojanavistīrṇā śailakukṣiṣu saṃvṛtā.
yādhṛtā devadevena śaṅkareṇa mahātmanā .. 42.36 ..
1.42.d:
रम्या योजनविस्तीर्णा शैलकुक्षिषु संवृता।
याधृता देवदेवेन शङ्करेण महात्मना ॥ 42.36 ॥
1.42.m: Charming, a yojana wide, surrounded within the recesses of mountains, / it was held by the great-souled Śaṅkara, god of gods. 42.36

1.42.s:
pāvanī dvijaśārdūla ghorāṇāmapi pāpmanām.
śaṅkarasyāṅkasaṃsparśānmahādevasya dhīmataḥ.
dviguṇaṃ pavitrasalilā sarvaloke mahānadī .. 42.37 ..
1.42.d:
पावनी द्विजशार्दूल घोराणामपि पाप्मनाम्।
शङ्करस्याङ्कसंस्पर्शान्महादेवस्य धीमतः।
द्विगुणं पवित्रसलिला सर्वलोके महानदी ॥ 42.37 ॥
1.42.m: Purifier even of dread sinners, O tiger among the twice-born, / from the contact with the lap of Śaṅkara, the wise Mahādeva, / that great river became doubly pure in its waters throughout all the worlds. 42.37

1.42.s:
anuśailaṃ samantācca nirgatā bahubhirmukhaiḥ.
atho'nyenābhidhānena khyātā nadyaḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 42.38 ..
1.42.d:
अनुशैलं समन्ताच्च निर्गता बहुभिर्मुखैः।
अथोऽन्येनाभिधानेन ख्याता नद्यः सहस्रशः ॥ 42.38 ॥
1.42.m: Issuing along the mountains on all sides through many mouths, / it is known by thousands of rivers under other names. 42.38

1.42.s:
tasmāddhimavato gaṅgā gatā sā tu mahānadī.
evaṃ gaṅgeti nāmnādiprakāśā siddhasevitā .. 42.39 ..
1.42.d:
तस्माद्धिमवतो गङ्गा गता सा तु महानदी।
एवं गङ्गेति नाम्नादिप्रकाशा सिद्धसेविता ॥ 42.39 ॥
1.42.m: From that Himavat, that great river went forth as the Gaṅgā; / thus renowned under the primary name Gaṅgā, it is frequented by siddhas. 42.39

1.42.s:
dhanyāste sattamā deśā yatra gaṅgā mahānadī.
rudrasāddhyānilādityairjuṣṭatoyā yaśasvatī .. 42.40 ..
1.42.d:
धन्यास्ते सत्तमा देशा यत्र गङ्गा महानदी।
रुद्रसाद्ध्यानिलादित्यैर्जुष्टतोया यशस्वती ॥ 42.40 ॥
1.42.m: Blessed are those most excellent lands where the great river Gaṅgā is, / whose waters are frequented by the Rudras, Sādhyas, winds, and Ādityas, renowned for its glory. 42.40

1.42.s:
mahāpādaṃ pravakṣyāmi merorapi hi paścimam.
nānāratnākāraṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyakṛdbhirniṣevitam .. 42.41 ..
1.42.d:
महापादं प्रवक्ष्यामि मेरोरपि हि पश्चिमम्।
नानारत्नाकारं पुण्यं पुण्यकृद्भिर्निषेवितम् ॥ 42.41 ॥
1.42.m: I shall tell of Meru's great western buttress also, / rich in mines of diverse jewels, sacred, frequented by performers of holy deeds,

1.42.s:
vipulaṃ śailarājānaṃ vipulodarakandaram .
nitambakuñja kaṭakairvimalairmmaṇḍitodaram .. 42.42 ..
1.42.d:
विपुलं शैलराजानं विपुलोदरकन्दरम् ।
नितम्बकुञ्ज कटकैर्विमलैर्म्मण्डितोदरम् ॥ 42.42 ॥
1.42.m: the great king of mountains, Vipula, vast in its caves and recesses, / its interior adorned with spotless flanks, bowers, and ridges.

1.42.s:
api yā tryambakasyaiṣā tridaśaiḥ sevitodakā.
vāyuvegā gatābhogā lateva bhrāmitā punaḥ .. 42.43 ..
1.42.d:
अपि या त्र्यम्बकस्यैषा त्रिदशैः सेवितोदका।
वायुवेगा गताभोगा लतेव भ्रामिता पुनः ॥ 42.43 ॥
1.42.m: The [stream] that belongs to Tryambaka, whose waters are enjoyed by the gods, / impelled by the wind, expanding in curves, circled like a creeper;

1.42.s:
merukūṭataṭādbhraṣṭā prahataiḥ svāditodakā.
vistīryyamāṇasalilā nirmmalāṃśukasannibhā .. 42.44 ..
1.42.d:
मेरुकूटतटाद्भ्रष्टा प्रहतैः स्वादितोदका।
विस्तीर्य्यमाणसलिला निर्म्मलांशुकसन्निभा ॥ 42.44 ॥
1.42.m: tumbling from the cliffs of Meru’s peaks, its waters tasted by the blessed, / its waters spreading wide, resembling a spotless garment.

1.42.s:
tasya kūṭe'mbaranadī siddhacāraṇasevitā .
pradakṣiṇamathāvṛtya patitā sā tu gāminī .. 42.45 ..
1.42.d:
तस्य कूटेऽम्बरनदी सिद्धचारणसेविता ।
प्रदक्षिणमथावृत्य पतिता सा तु गामिनी ॥ 42.45 ॥
1.42.m: Upon its peak, that river of the sky, frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas, / having turned clockwise, fell, flowing on,

1.42.s:
devabhrājaṃ mahābhrājaṃ savaibhrājaṃ mahāvanam.
plāvayantī mahābhāgā nānāpuṣpaphalodakā .. 42.46 ..
1.42.d:
देवभ्राजं महाभ्राजं सवैभ्राजं महावनम्।
प्लावयन्ती महाभागा नानापुष्पफलोदका ॥ 42.46 ॥
1.42.m: flooding the great Devabhrāja, the Mahābhrāja, and the great forest Vaibhrāja, / the illustrious river, with its waters bearing diverse flowers and fruits.

1.42.s:
pradakṣiṇaṃ prakurvāṇā nānāvanavibhūṣitā.
praviṣṭā paśvimasaraḥ sitodaṃ vimalodakam .. 42.47 ..
1.42.d:
प्रदक्षिणं प्रकुर्वाणा नानावनविभूषिता।
प्रविष्टा पश्विमसरः सितोदं विमलोदकम् ॥ 42.47 ॥
1.42.m: Circling clockwise, adorned with diverse forests, / it entered the western lake Sitoda, of spotless waters.

1.42.s:
sā sitodādviniṣkrāntā supakṣaṃ parvvataṃ gatā.
supakṣatastu puṇyodāttato devarṣisevitā .. 42.48 ..
1.42.d:
सा सितोदाद्विनिष्क्रान्ता सुपक्षं पर्व्वतं गता।
सुपक्षतस्तु पुण्योदात्ततो देवर्षिसेविता ॥ 42.48 ॥
1.42.m: Flowing forth from Sitoda, it went to Mount Supakṣa; / from Supakṣa, possessing holy waters, frequented by divine seers,

1.42.s:
supakṣakūṭataṭagā tasmācca saṃśitodakā.
nipapāta mahābhāgā ramaṇyaṃ śikhiparvvatam .. 42.49 ..
1.42.d:
सुपक्षकूटतटगा तस्माच्च संशितोदका।
निपपात महाभागा रमण्यं शिखिपर्व्वतम् ॥ 42.49 ॥
1.42.m: flowing along the cliffs and peaks of Supakṣa, and of purified waters from there, / the illustrious river fell upon the delightful Śikhi mountain;

1.42.s:
śikheśca parvatāt kaṅkaṃ kaṅkādvaidūryyaparvvatam.
vaidūryyāt kapilaṃ śailaṃ tasmācca gandhamādanam .. 42.50 ..
1.42.d:
शिखेश्च पर्वतात् कङ्कं कङ्काद्वैदूर्य्यपर्व्वतम्।
वैदूर्य्यात् कपिलं शैलं तस्माच्च गन्धमादनम् ॥ 42.50 ॥
1.42.m: and from Mount Śikhi to Kaṅka; from Kaṅka to Mount Vaidūrya; / from Vaidūrya to Mount Kapila; and from that to Gandhamādana;

1.42.s:
tasmādgirivarāt prāptā piñjaraṃ varaparvvatam.
piñjarāt sarasaṃ yātā tasmācca kumudācalam .. 42.51 ..
1.42.d:
तस्माद्गिरिवरात् प्राप्ता पिञ्जरं वरपर्व्वतम्।
पिञ्जरात् सरसं याता तस्माच्च कुमुदाचलम् ॥ 42.51 ॥
1.42.m: from that best of mountains it reached Piñjara, the excellent mountain; / from Piñjara it went to Sarasa, and from there to Mount Kumuda;

1.42.s:
madhumantaṃ janañcaiva mukuṭañca śiloccayam.
mukuṭācchailaśikharāt kṛṣṇaṃ yātā mahāgirim .. 42.52 ..
1.42.d:
मधुमन्तं जनञ्चैव मुकुटञ्च शिलोच्चयम्।
मुकुटाच्छैलशिखरात् कृष्णं याता महागिरिम् ॥ 42.52 ॥
1.42.m: to Madhumat, Jana, and the mountain Mukuṭa; / and from the mountain summit of Mukuṭa it went to the great mountain Kṛṣṇa;

1.42.s:
kṛṣṇāt śvetaṃ mahāśailaṃ mahānaganiṣevitam.
śvetāt sahasraśikharaṃ śailendraṃ patitā punaḥ .. 42.53 ..
1.42.d:
कृष्णात् श्वेतं महाशैलं महानगनिषेवितम्।
श्वेतात् सहस्रशिखरं शैलेन्द्रं पतिता पुनः ॥ 42.53 ॥
1.42.m: from Kṛṣṇa to the great mountain Śveta, frequented by great elephants; / from Śveta it fell again onto Sahasraśikhara, king of mountains.

1.42.s:
anekābhiḥ sravantībhirāpyāyitajalā śivā .
evaṃ śailasahasrāṇi sādayantī mahānadī.
pārijāte mahāśaile nipapātāśugāminī .. 42.54 ..
1.42.d:
अनेकाभिः स्रवन्तीभिराप्यायितजला शिवा ।
एवं शैलसहस्राणि सादयन्ती महानदी।
पारिजाते महाशैले निपपाताशुगामिनी ॥ 42.54 ॥
1.42.m: Swollen with waters by many flowing streams, auspicious, / thus splitting thousands of mountains, the great river, swift-moving, / tumbled down onto the great mountain Pārijāta.

1.42.s:
anekanirjharanadī guhāsānuṣu rājate.
tasya kukṣiṣvanekāsu bhrāntatoyā taraṅgiṇī .. 42.55 ..
1.42.d:
अनेकनिर्झरनदी गुहासानुषु राजते।
तस्य कुक्षिष्वनेकासु भ्रान्ततोया तरङ्गिणी ॥ 42.55 ॥
1.42.m: Rich with many cascade-rivers, it shines among the caves and ridges; / the river, its waters swirling within its many hollows,

1.42.s:
vyāhanyamānasaṃvegā gaṇḍaśailairanekaśaḥ.
saṃvidyamānasalilā gatā ca dharaṇītale .. 42.56 ..
1.42.d:
व्याहन्यमानसंवेगा गण्डशैलैरनेकशः।
संविद्यमानसलिला गता च धरणीतले ॥ 42.56 ॥
1.42.m: its momentum shattered many times by boulders, / its waters surging, reached the surface of the earth.

1.42.s:
ketumālaṃ mahādvīpaṃ nānāmleccha gaṇairyutam .
plāvayantī mahābhāgā prayātā paścimārṇavam .. 42.57 ..
1.42.d:
केतुमालं महाद्वीपं नानाम्लेच्छ गणैर्युतम् ।
प्लावयन्ती महाभागा प्रयाता पश्चिमार्णवम् ॥ 42.57 ॥
1.42.m: Flooding the great continent of Ketumāla, populated by diverse barbarian hordes, / the illustrious river departed to the western ocean.

1.42.s:
suvarṇacitrapārśve tu supārśve'pyuttare girau .
merościtramahāpāde mahāsattvaniṣevite .. 42.58 ..
1.42.d:
सुवर्णचित्रपार्श्वे तु सुपार्श्वेऽप्युत्तरे गिरौ ।
मेरोश्चित्रमहापादे महासत्त्वनिषेविते ॥ 42.58 ॥
1.42.m: Now on the flank variegated with gold, and on the northern mountain Supārśva, / the variegated great buttress of Meru, inhabited by great beings,

1.42.s:
merukūṭataṭādbhraṣṭā pavaneneritodakā.
anekābhogavakrāṅgī kṣipyamāṇā nabhastale .. 42.59 ..
1.42.d:
मेरुकूटतटाद्भ्रष्टा पवनेनेरितोदका।
अनेकाभोगवक्राङ्गी क्षिप्यमाणा नभस्तले ॥ 42.59 ॥
1.42.m: tumbling from the cliffs of Meru’s peaks, its waters stirred by the wind, / its body curving in many expanses, cast through the sky,

1.42.s:
ṣaṣṭiyojanasāhasre nirālambe'mbare śubhe.
vikīryamāṇā māleva nipapāta mahānadī .. 42.60 ..
1.42.d:
षष्टियोजनसाहस्रे निरालम्बेऽम्बरे शुभे।
विकीर्यमाणा मालेव निपपात महानदी ॥ 42.60 ॥
1.42.m: scattered like a garland across sixty thousand yojanas / in the supportless, auspicious sky, the great river fell.

1.42.s:
evaṃ kūṭataṭairbhraṣṭā naikairdevarṣisevitaiḥ.
vikīryamāṇasalilā naikapuṣpoḍupotkacā .. 42.61 ..
1.42.d:
एवं कूटतटैर्भ्रष्टा नैकैर्देवर्षिसेवितैः।
विकीर्यमाणसलिला नैकपुष्पोडुपोत्कचा ॥ 42.61 ॥
1.42.m: Thus fallen from cliff-peaks frequented by numerous divine seers, / with scattering waters, bristling with raft-like petals of diverse flowers,

1.42.s:
nānāratnavanoddeśamaraṇyaṃ saviturvvanam.
mahāvanaṃ mahābhāgā plāvayantī pradakṣiṇam .. 42.62 ..
1.42.d:
नानारत्नवनोद्देशमरण्यं सवितुर्व्वनम्।
महावनं महाभागा प्लावयन्ती प्रदक्षिणम् ॥ 42.62 ॥
1.42.m: circling clockwise and flooding the region of forests with various jewels, / the wilderness of the Sun, the great forest, the illustrious river,

1.42.s:
sarovaraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ mahābhāganiṣevitam.
tatrāviveśa kalyāṇī mahābhadraṃ sitodakā .. 42.63 ..
1.42.d:
सरोवरं महापुण्यं महाभागनिषेवितम्।
तत्राविवेश कल्याणी महाभद्रं सितोदका ॥ 42.63 ॥
1.42.m: the great, holy lake, frequented by the illustrious, / there the auspicious river of white waters entered the Mahābhadra.

1.42.s:
bhadrasometi nāmnā hi mahāpārā mahājavā.
mahānadī mahāpuṇyā mahābhadrā vinirgatā .. 42.64 ..
1.42.d:
भद्रसोमेति नाम्ना हि महापारा महाजवा।
महानदी महापुण्या महाभद्रा विनिर्गता ॥ 42.64 ॥
1.42.m: Under the name Bhadrasomā indeed, of vast banks and immense speed, / a great, most holy river, Mahābhadrā, emerged.

1.42.s:
naikanirjharavaprāḍhyā śaṃkhakūṭataṭe tu sā.
tatra kūṭe giritaṭe nipapātāśugāminī .. 42.65 ..
1.42.d:
नैकनिर्झरवप्राढ्या शंखकूटतटे तु सा।
तत्र कूटे गिरितटे निपपाताशुगामिनी ॥ 42.65 ॥
1.42.m: Rich with many cascade-terraces upon the cliffs of Śaṅkhakūṭa, / on that peak, upon the mountain cliff, it fell, swift-moving.

1.42.s:
śaṃkhakūṭataṭādbhraṣṭā papāta vṛṣaparvvatam.
vṛṣaparvvatādvatsagiriṃ nāgaśailaṃ tato gatā .. 42.66 ..
1.42.d:
शंखकूटतटाद्भ्रष्टा पपात वृषपर्व्वतम्।
वृषपर्व्वताद्वत्सगिरिं नागशैलं ततो गता ॥ 42.66 ॥
1.42.m: Tumbling from the cliff of Śaṅkhakūṭa, it fell to Mount Vṛṣa; / from Mount Vṛṣa it went to Mount Vatsa, and then to Mount Nāga;

1.42.s:
tasmānnīlaṃ nagaśreṣṭhaṃ saṃprāptā varṣaparvvatam.
nīlāt kapiñjalañcaiva indranīlaṃ ca nimnagā .. 42.67 ..
1.42.d:
तस्मान्नीलं नगश्रेष्ठं संप्राप्ता वर्षपर्व्वतम्।
नीलात् कपिञ्जलञ्चैव इन्द्रनीलं च निम्नगा ॥ 42.67 ॥
1.42.m: from there the river reached Nīla, best of mountains, the boundary mountain; / and from Nīla to Kapiñjala and Indranīla.

1.42.s:
tataḥ paraṃ mahānīlaṃ hemaśrṛṅgañca sā yayau .
hemaśrṛṅgādgatā śvetaṃ śvetācca sunagaṃ yayau .. 42.68 ..
1.42.d:
ततः परं महानीलं हेमश्रृङ्गञ्च सा ययौ ।
हेमश्रृङ्गाद्गता श्वेतं श्वेताच्च सुनगं ययौ ॥ 42.68 ॥
1.42.m: Beyond that it went to Mahānīla and Hemaśṛṅga; / from Hemaśṛṅga it went to Śveta, and from Śveta it went to Sunaga;

1.42.s:
sunagāt śataśrṛṅgañca saṃprāptā sā mahānadī.
śataśrṛṅgānmahāśailaṃ puṣkaraṃ puṣpamaṇḍitam .. 42.69 ..
1.42.d:
सुनगात् शतश्रृङ्गञ्च संप्राप्ता सा महानदी।
शतश्रृङ्गान्महाशैलं पुष्करं पुष्पमण्डितम् ॥ 42.69 ॥
1.42.m: and from Sunaga that great river reached Śataśṛṅga; / from Śataśṛṅga to the great mountain Puṣkara, adorned with blossoms;

1.42.s:
puṣkarācca mahāśailaṃ dvirājaṃ sumahābalam .
varāhaparvvataṃ tasmānmayūrañca śiloccayam .. 42.70 ..
1.42.d:
पुष्कराच्च महाशैलं द्विराजं सुमहाबलम् ।
वराहपर्व्वतं तस्मान्मयूरञ्च शिलोच्चयम् ॥ 42.70 ॥
1.42.m: and from Puṣkara to the great mountain Dvirāja of exceeding strength; / from there to Mount Varāha, and to the mountain Mayūra;

1.42.s:
mayūrāccaikaśikharaṃ kandarodaramaṇḍitam .
jārudhiṃ śaila śikharaṃ nipapātāśugāminī .. 42.71 ..
1.42.d:
मयूराच्चैकशिखरं कन्दरोदरमण्डितम् ।
जारुधिं शैल शिखरं निपपाताशुगामिनी ॥ 42.71 ॥
1.42.m: and from Mayūra, adorned with caves and hollows, to the single-peaked mountain summit, / Jārudhi, the swift-moving river fell.

1.42.s:
evaṃ girisahasrāṇi dārayantī mahānadī.
triśrṛṅgaṃ śrṛṅgakalilaṃ maryādāparvataṃ gatā .. 42.72 ..
1.42.d:
एवं गिरिसहस्राणि दारयन्ती महानदी।
त्रिश्रृङ्गं श्रृङ्गकलिलं मर्यादापर्वतं गता ॥ 42.72 ॥
1.42.m: Thus splitting thousands of mountains, the great river / went to Triśṛṅga, thick with peaks, a boundary mountain.

1.42.s:
triśrṛṅgataṭavibhraṣṭā mahābhāganiṣevitā.
merukūṭataṭādbhraṣṭā pavaneneritodakā .. 42.73 ..
1.42.d:
त्रिश्रृङ्गतटविभ्रष्टा महाभागनिषेविता।
मेरुकूटतटाद्भ्रष्टा पवनेनेरितोदका ॥ 42.73 ॥
1.42.m: Tumbling from the cliffs of Triśṛṅga, frequented by the illustrious, / having fallen from the cliffs of Meru’s peaks, its waters stirred by the wind,

1.42.s:
viruddhaṃ parvatavaraṃ papāta vimalodakā.
plāvayantī mahābhāgā prayātā paścimārṇavam .. 42.74 ..
1.42.d:
विरुद्धं पर्वतवरं पपात विमलोदका।
प्लावयन्ती महाभागा प्रयाता पश्चिमार्णवम् ॥ 42.74 ॥
1.42.m: the river of spotless waters fell onto Viruddha, best of mountains; / flooding [the land], the illustrious river departed to the western ocean.

1.42.s: suvarṇabhuvi pārśve tu supārśvepyuttare girau ..
1.42.d: सुवर्णभुवि पार्श्वे तु सुपार्श्वेप्युत्तरे गिरौ ॥
1.42.m:
On the golden ground at the side, on the northern mountain Supārśva,
on the variegated great foot of Meru, frequented by great creatures—

1.42.s: merośvitre mahāpāde mahāsattvaniṣevite .. 42.75 ..
1.42.d: मेरोश्वित्रे महापादे महासत्त्वनिषेविते ॥ 42.75 ॥

1.42.s:
kandarodaravibhraṣṭā tasmādapi taraṅgiṇī.
naikabhogā papātorvīṃ citrapuṣpoḍhupotkacā .. 42.76 ..
1.42.d:
कन्दरोदरविभ्रष्टा तस्मादपि तरङ्गिणी।
नैकभोगा पपातोर्वीं चित्रपुष्पोढुपोत्कचा ॥ 42.76 ॥
1.42.m: falling from within its caves and hollows, the stream from that too, / having many expanses, bristling with raft-like variegated blossoms, fell to the earth.

1.42.s:
plāvayantī pramuditā uttarān sā kurūn śivā.
mahādvīpasya madhyena prayātā sottarārṇavam .. 42.77 ..
1.42.d:
प्लावयन्ती प्रमुदिता उत्तरान् सा कुरून् शिवा।
महाद्वीपस्य मध्येन प्रयाता सोत्तरार्णवम् ॥ 42.77 ॥
1.42.m: Joyfully flooding the Northern Kurus, the auspicious river, / through the middle of the great continent, departed to the northern ocean.

1.42.s:
evaṃ tāstu mahānadyaścatasro vimalodakāḥ.
mahāgiritaṭabhraṣṭāḥ saṃprayātāścaturdiśam .. 42.78 ..
1.42.d:
एवं तास्तु महानद्यश्चतस्रो विमलोदकाः।
महागिरितटभ्रष्टाः संप्रयाताश्चतुर्दिशम् ॥ 42.78 ॥
1.42.m: Thus those four great rivers of spotless waters, / tumbling from the cliffs of the great mountain, flowed forth toward the four directions.

1.42.s:
tatseyaṃ kathitaprāyā pṛthivī bahuvistarā.
